plugins.description: v0.7.117: wires the 3rd taintguard trigger — "this turn consumed cross-project lessons" — into `condukt lessons record-retrieval`. On the same non-empty-hit condition the existing retrieval-ledger `hit` flag already uses, the handler now calls `taintguard::state::mark(&cwd, &run, "lessons")` (new `taintguard` path dependency, mirroring the existing `blastguard`/`overwatch` deps; taintguard itself is unchanged), tainting the session so taintguard's PreToolUse `gate` downgrades write-class tools for the rest of the turn — mirroring the existing web/external-read triggers. A zero-hit search stays a no-op (preserves the empty `lessons_context: []` contract); a failed `mark` is `eprintln!`'d and does not fail the command (record-retrieval is a soft injection helper, mirrors taintguard's own fail-soft mark-side degrade — its `check`'s writability probe is the real backstop, not this call's `Err`). New `tests/lessons_taint_trigger.rs` confirms RED (no taint) with the mark call disabled and GREEN once wired, plus an anti-vacuity zero-hit case (stays Clean) and a regression on the unchanged retrieval-ledger/lessons_context shape. v0.7.116: closes an injection fail-open in `verify.rs`'s four non-interactive subprocess-exec seams (`launch_and_reflux`, `launch_server_and_probe`, `launch_in_container`, `run_check`) — each gated only on `blastguard::model::Decision::Deny`, so a blastguard `Decision::Ask` verdict (unresolvable/high-blast constructs, e.g. an unrecognised wrapper head in front of a destructive tail) fell through the `if let Deny` match untouched and reached `sh -c`/`docker run`, even though `Decision::Ask` is only a safe answer when a human is present to resolve it (blastguard model.rs) and these callers are ALWAYS non-interactive automation. Each seam now applies `.hardened()` to the detector's verdict before matching, folding `Ask` into `Deny` so it rides the existing fail-closed refusal branch unchanged (same reason string, same `CheckResult{passed:false,exit:-1}`/fail-soft-launch-verdict shape); `Allow` and pre-existing `Deny` behavior are untouched. New `tests/gate_exec_cli.rs` coverage pins a concrete `Decision::Ask` input (`my-cleanup-wrapper rm -rf /some/path`, blastguard's ASK-2 unknown-wrapper case) and drives it through the `checks[]` oracle CLI (`condukt verify checks`): confirmed RED by transiently reverting the `run_check` seam (observed `exit:127`, proving `sh -c` was genuinely invoked pre-fix) and GREEN after restoring (`exit:-1`, refused before spawn); an anti-vacuity control (`true`, `Decision::Allow`) confirms the hardening does not over-block legitimate checks, and a `Decision::Deny` regression case (`rm -rf /`) stays refused. `cargo test -p condukt` (all suites, 850 tests) green; `cargo clippy -p condukt --all-targets` clean. v0.7.112: doc-comment fix (CLAUDE.md §4) — v0.7.111 inserted the new `phase_span_secs`/`fmt_span`/`print_timings` helpers in the middle of `record_runs`'s rustdoc block, so `record_runs`'s summary sentence ("Record completed runs' outcomes to fugu-router…") had migrated onto `phase_span_secs` and `record_runs` was left starting mid-thought at "Soft dependency: …". Re-attached the summary to `record_runs`; no behavior change. v0.7.111: per-phase timestamps on `TaskState` + a `state timings` subcommand (measurement only). Five new `Option<i64>` fields (`worker_started_at`/`worker_ended_at`/`verifier_started_at`/`verifier_ended_at`/`merge_completed_at`), each `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if=Option::is_none)]` so pre-existing run-state JSON still deserializes and tasks without them serialize unchanged. Each is stamped set-once by a REAL orchestrator transition the engine already performs: `state set --status running` → worker start, the first `--status done` → worker end + verifier start, `--status verified`/`failed` → verifier end, and a successful `worktree merge --run --task` → merge complete (new optional `--run`/`--task` flags on `worktree merge`; a bare merge is unchanged). New `condukt state timings --run <RID> [--json]` prints the per-task phase breakdown; an unmeasured phase is rendered as an explicit `unmeasured` marker (text) / `null` (JSON), NEVER as 0 seconds, so never-measured stays distinguishable from completed-instantly — the same tri-state norm as fugu-router's `duration_secs`. Companion to fugu-router 0.1.25: `record_runs` now forwards `--duration` ONLY when the derived span is strictly positive (a same-second task yields `Some(0.0)`, which fugu-router 0.1.25 now rejects; omitting records it as unmeasured). Measurement only — no pipeline-shortening change this cycle; none of the new fields are consulted by scheduling/routing. New `tests/phase_timings_e2e.rs` drives the real CLI transitions (running/done/failed/merge) and the timings output (unmeasured≠0, legacy JSON still loads); RED→GREEN recorded via tdd --task t4. v0.7.110: closed the `started_at` stamping gap — `TaskState.started_at` was stamped ONLY by the explicit `--status running` transition (main.rs), so any orchestration path that settled a task without passing through `running` (e.g. a branch/worktree assigned then settled straight to done, or a reconcile-promoted task) left `started_at` — and therefore the derived `duration_secs` — None, so ~71/120 recent episodes had no measured duration. New `state::stamp_started_at_if_unset` stamps `started_at` at the earliest defensible point (set-once, never overwriting): the first `running` transition OR the first time a worktree/branch is assigned, both of which provably precede worker execution. The `running` edge is now routed through the same set-once helper so a re-dispatch no longer resets and shrinks a real duration. Where a task genuinely has no start information (a reconcile-promoted task that never got a worktree/branch) `started_at` stays None → duration None, NEVER a fabricated 0.0; the existing tri-state duration derivation in state.rs (None started_at yields None duration) is untouched and pinned. New `tests/started_at_e2e.rs` drives the real CLI paths (branch assigned without a running edge now stamps; reconcile without start info keeps None; set-once not overwritten; legacy run-state lacking the field still reads); RED→GREEN recorded via tdd --task t2. v0.7.109: closed an F→P oracle fail-open (backlog 22b69f6a) — `oracle::check_oracle`'s top-of-function exemption fired on `!requires_oracle || reproduction_tests.is_none()`, so a fix/feature task (`requires_oracle:true`) that did not DECLARE `reproduction_tests` was exempted from the Fail→Pass gate even when real tdd RED→GREEN proofs existed. Narrowed the guard to `!requires_oracle` alone: a fix/feature task is now ALWAYS consulted against `tdd` regardless of a declared `reproduction_tests` (missing declarations degrade to the tdd `unknown`/spawn-Err paths, never a free pass). The `reproduction_tests` param is retained for call-site signature stability (renamed `_reproduction_tests`) but is no longer a gate switch; the doc comment and exempt `reason` (`"not a fix/feature task"`, no longer `"or no reproduction_tests"`) were updated in the same commit; the tdd-spawn/spawn-Err (`"a missing checker is not a passing checker"`) branches are unchanged. v0.7.108: added a must-ask-human / untestable clamp to the graded-autonomy policy (backlog 903a0d28) — new `policy::decide_untestable(risk, reversibility, confidence)` mirrors `decide_conflict_resolution`: it calls `decide` and clamps an `Auto` verdict up to `Escalate`, passing `Escalate`/`Block` through unchanged (pure, total, no opt-in path back to Auto), so CLAUDE.md §2's "if a thing cannot be meaningfully tested, ask the human" gate can never be auto-self-answered. Wired a `--untestable` bool flag into both `policy decide` and `policy answer` (mirrors `--conflict`); when set, the verdict is computed by `decide_untestable`, so an otherwise-`auto` untestable decision falls through to a real AskUserQuestion (exit 2, escalate JSON, never journaled). `--untestable` takes precedence over `--conflict` (both clamp Auto→Escalate identically). Everything downstream is unchanged. v0.7.107: the GHA removal landed across two commits (the second re-touched condukt src, so the bump-on-change gate required a second micro bump); functionally identical to v0.7.106. v0.7.106: removed the GitHub-Actions-CI-status-consuming code (GHA is banned repo-wide, CLAUDE.md; its workflow files are already gone) — deleted `src/ci.rs` entirely (the `gh pr checks`/`gh run list --json` output parser plus `CiConclusion`/`CiVerdict` state machine that existed solely to consume GHA CI conclusions) and removed the `condukt pr poll` subcommand from `main.rs` (its `PrAction::Poll` variant, handler, and the merge-only-when-CI-green flow), since that subcommand's entire purpose was gated on GHA CI state. Kept `src/pr.rs` and `condukt pr create` (`gh pr create` with no CI-conclusion gating — general PR creation, independent of GHA). Also gutted `scripts/test_prepush_hook.py`'s now-stale chronic-red-CI test suite (the check it tested was already removed from `.githooks/pre-push`) and replaced it with coverage for the hook's surviving checks (gate-bypass block, rollout advisory). v0.7.104: `record_runs` now emits a SECOND fugu-router episode with `role=verifier` alongside the existing worker episode, whenever a task carried `state set --verifier-model` (reusing the same title/files/class/done_criteria/status; resolving cost/tokens via `--verifier-agent-id` through the same `resolve_agent_cost`/`resolve_agent_tokens` exact-match path the worker episode already used). Builds on v0.7.103's verifier_model/verifier_cost_usd/verifier_agent_id fields toward hypothesis f5f9522a. `fugu-router record --role`/`Episode.role` already existed and needed no change. New e2e test `record_run_emits_worker_and_verifier_episodes_when_verifier_model_set` asserts exactly 2 episodes (worker+verifier) for a task with a verifier model and exactly 1 (worker only) for a task without one. v0.7.103: merges the verifier-fields-state-cli task (TaskState/RecordSpec gain measurement-only verifier_model/verifier_cost_usd/verifier_agent_id, plus state set --verifier-model/--verifier-cost/--verifier-agent-id) toward hypothesis f5f9522a's future verification. v0.7.100: fixed a PATH-env test race (backlog b0db2bff) — `oracle.rs` had its own module-local `ORACLE_PATH_ENV_LOCK` serializing only its own PATH-mutating tests; `main.rs`'s `flag_supplied_but_probe_unusable_falls_back` mutated PATH without taking any lock, and tests that spawn real `git` (e.g. `repo_commit::tests::first_unstaged_modification_is_not_misread_as_staged`, via `worktree::git`) took no lock at all, so a concurrent PATH mutation could transiently break their git spawn. Reproduced empirically: 3/15 full-suite runs under 16 test threads flaked before the fix (2 distinct real failures). New shared `env_lock::PATH_ENV_LOCK` (`RwLock<()>`, not a `Mutex`) — PATH mutators (oracle.rs, main.rs) take the write side; `worktree::run_git_bounded_with` (the single git-spawn choke point used by every git-shelling test in the crate) takes the read side, so concurrent git spawns don't serialize against each other but always exclude a mutation window. 20/20 repeats of the same repro loop green after the fix; full `cargo test -p condukt` suite green x3; fmt/clippy clean. v0.7.99: fixed `state::all_runs`/`active_worktree_for_path` misparsing non-RunState sidecars in the per-project state dir as corrupt run states (backlog 1af91627). Only `<run_id>.decomposition.json` was excluded; `<run_id>.checkpoints.json` (checkpoint history) and the bare `claims.json` (cross-run claim registry) were fed to `serde_json::from_str::<RunState>` and logged as "unparseable run state" — reproduced live via `condukt state record-run --all` (8 `.checkpoints.json` + 1 `claims.json` = 9 spurious warnings). Grepped the file for every other bare-filename sidecar sharing the same directory (`precedents.json`, `escalations.json`, `execution-state.json`) and excluded those too via a new shared `is_run_state_sidecar()` helper used by both functions, rather than patching just the 2 observed symptoms. New regression test `all_runs_skips_all_known_sidecars_without_warning` fixtures one valid RunState plus all 6 known sidecar shapes and asserts `all_runs` returns exactly the one valid run. v0.7.98: internal-only refactor — `verify::checks_verdict`'s computation now routes through `harness_core::verdict::{Determination, Verdict}` (an empty results slice becomes `Determination::Undetermined`, a non-empty slice becomes `Determination::Known` with per-index failure reasons, adjudicated via `Verdict::adjudicate`), then translates back to `ChecksVerdict` at the return boundary. `ChecksVerdict`/`CheckReport`'s public shape and `Serialize`/`Deserialize` derives are unchanged (a `Verdict` can never derive `Deserialize` — see harness-core's `Evidence` witness — so `ChecksVerdict` stays its own serializable shadow type). All pre-existing checks-verdict tests pass unmodified. Skipped the optional per-check-failure-reason threading (naming which check failed): `checks_verdict` is directly tested with bare `&[bool]` literals, so giving it access to `check.cmd` would mean either breaking that tested signature or duplicating logic between it and `run_checks` — both out of scope for an internal-only refactor. v0.7.97: `review_brief.rs`'s `source_label()` match arm now covers the 6 new `ViolationSource` variants (Donegate/Reviewgate/Tdd/Budgetguard/Autoflow/Ctxrot) added to overwatch's cross-gate ledger; no behavior change to review-brief rendering. v0.7.95: fixed a real fail-closed-refusal bug in `repo commit` found live while committing an unrelated blastguard fix — `worktree::git`'s shared output formatter used to `.trim()` the WHOLE stdout blob of every git invocation, not just its trailing newline. `git status --porcelain`'s first line for an unstaged modification is ` M path` (a leading space that is the semantically meaningful 'not staged' status column, not incidental whitespace); because that space sat at byte 0 of the whole blob, the blanket `.trim()` ate it, corrupting only the FIRST line. `repo_commit::staged_paths` then read the corrupted line's first byte as the file-status char (neither `' '` nor `'?'`) and wrongly reported an ordinary unstaged edit as already-staged foreign content, and its `path[3..]` slice then cut one byte too many off the path itself (observed live as `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` reported as `claude-plugin/marketplace.json`, missing its leading dot). This made `condukt repo commit` refuse to commit ANY task whose first `git status --porcelain` entry happened to be a plain unstaged modification. Fixed by changing the shared formatter to `.trim_end()` (strips only the trailing newline git always appends). New regression test `repo_commit::tests::first_unstaged_modification_is_not_misread_as_staged` reproduces the exact incident shape, confirmed RED before the fix and GREEN after; full `cargo test -p condukt` suite (721 tests) still green. v0.7.94: fixes a defect the section-8 main-tree guard found in itself - it blocked the real `git merge --no-ff` of its own branch into main. The integration exclusion keyed only off on-disk markers, and measured, git writes MERGE_HEAD only when a merge STOPS (a conflict or --no-commit); a merge that is succeeding fires `.githooks/pre-merge-commit` with no marker anywhere, so the exclusion section 8 requires never fired on the path that matters and the gate made the worktree workflow undischargeable. `.githooks/pre-merge-commit` now declares the invocation context (CONDUKT_GIT_HOOK) across its exec, and the guard honors it only when git's own GIT_REFLOG_ACTION corroborates it - git sets that for a merge and leaves it unset for an ordinary commit, so forging the declaration alone on a plain commit excludes nothing (pinned by a test). The on-disk detection is kept, not replaced: a conflicted merge finished by hand still arrives at pre-commit with MERGE_HEAD present. Every integration pass now prints what excluded it, so an exclusion firing wrongly is visible in the output of the command it let through. The regression test drives the real path (real temp repo, real --no-ff merge, this repository's own pre-merge-commit copied verbatim, peer session injected) and fails without the fix. v0.7.93: prose fix on the section-8 main-tree guard - the block message and the pre-commit remediation hint named `condukt worktree add`, a subcommand that does not exist; the real one is `condukt worktree create`. v0.7.92: machine enforcement of CLAUDE.md section 8 (do not share-edit the primary working tree). New `condukt guard main-tree` (crates/condukt/src/maintree.rs) refuses a commit made from the SHARED primary working tree while another session is live, and .githooks/pre-commit runs it as a BLOCKING check - the authority to stop a commit stays local, no CI job and no GitHub ruleset. The decision is a pure function over injectable observations returning harness_core::verdict::Verdict, so cannot-determine (overwatch absent, non-zero exit, unparseable liveness output, IO failure) resolves to a BLOCK with exit 2 rather than to 'nobody is live'; a violation exits 1. It is not a detector that always fires: it passes from a linked worktree, during an integration (MERGE_HEAD / rebase / cherry-pick / revert, which section 8 explicitly permits in the main tree), with nothing staged, and when neither liveness input (overwatch status --json, backlog lock status) reports a peer session. The escape hatch is session-scoped by construction: CONDUKT_MAINTREE_OVERRIDE='<reason>' with a non-blank reason, echoed to stderr, never a project-root skip file (which is consumed once and would wave through another session's gate); the override exits 0 without rewriting the recorded verdict. 17 unit tests plus a 12-case CLI suite over a real temp repo and a real linked worktree, with the peer session injected via stub liveness binaries. v0.7.91: eradicates the last fail-OPEN callers of the repo-primary lock (backlog 66557497). v0.7.90 made `repo commit` REFUSE when the lock cannot be held, but the five remaining primary-repo mutators still called the fail-soft `lock::acquire_repo_primary` (= `RunLock::acquire`), which on a 10s timeout / IO error / serialization error printed a warning, handed back an UNHELD guard and let the caller proceed UNLOCKED - so a degraded lock on any of them raced the newly-serialized commit path and defeated the serialization it had just established (the recurring 'mirror gap': a fix lands on one path, its twin keeps the old behavior). `acquire_repo_primary`/`_loaded` now return `Result<RunLock>` and the fail-soft entry points `RunLock::acquire`/`acquire_with_deadline` are DELETED, so an unheld guard is no longer representable outside the module: every acquisition is `Option`/`Result` and cannot-determine must be handled. All five sites REFUSE: `worktree::merge` and `worktree::resolve_merge` (checkout of the default branch plus a merge commit in the shared primary working tree), `worktree::create` (the lock spans `worktree prune` plus the stale-ref `branch -D` plus `worktree add`, so unlocked it could force-delete a ref a peer merge is landing), `worktree::discard` (the unrecoverable `branch -D`), and `worktree cleanup` in main.rs (an unlocked prune can drop the admin entry a peer `worktree add` just published), whose orphan listing also moved INSIDE the critical section, closing a list-then-delete TOCTOU. No carve-outs: the bounded wait already IS the retry (a live holder is waited out for 10s, a dead holder reaped immediately), so reaching the deadline is genuine cannot-determine. Each site is pinned by its own fault-injected regression (a `state_dir` that is a regular FILE makes lock-dir creation fail deterministically) asserting both the refusal AND that no mutation happened: no merge landed, no worktree registered, no branch ref deleted. v0.7.90: closes condukt's shared main-working-tree hazard (backlog 15b682d2). The single-worktree / fast-path / serial main-tree commit used to be hand-rolled `git add <paths> && git commit` in the /condukt skill's shell, so NO in-process site held `lock::REPO_PRIMARY_LOCK_KEY` — two sessions sharing one index is the one conflict git cannot resolve by merging, and it was only masked by the coarse /flow backlog run.lock that per-task claiming removes. New `condukt repo commit --path <f>... -m <msg>` performs index-check -> `git add` -> `git commit` with the repo-scoped primary lock held across the whole cycle, joining the same serialization as `worktree merge`/`resolve-merge`/`worktree prune`. Every cannot-determine resolves restrictively (non-zero, HEAD unmoved): the lock uses `acquire_or_skip` so a timed-out/degraded acquisition REFUSES instead of proceeding unlocked, an empty/widening pathspec (`.`, glob, `-A`, `:` magic) is rejected, and foreign content already staged in the shared index is refused rather than swept into this task's commit. SKILL.md Phase 4.5.5/5A/5B now mandate `repo commit` and downgrade workers to `commit_mode: no-stage-no-commit` (workers never touch the shared index). Pinned by `tests/repo_commit_index_isolation.rs`, which races two real condukt processes in one working tree with a widened add->commit window and asserts each commit contains ONLY its own file. v0.7.89: cross-session namespacing for worktrees/branches (backlog 0213f7a9) — `condukt worktree create --run <RID>` puts the worktree at `<worktree_base>/<RID>-<topic>` and the branch at `<prefix>/<RID>/<name>`, so two CONCURRENT sessions that both emit the same per-run task id (`t1`) no longer aim at the identical dir and the identical branch ref. That collision previously bailed the second run out (`worktree path already exists` / `branch is already checked out`) and, worse, let `create()`'s stale-ref cleanup (`git branch -D`, guarded only by "not checked out in a LIVE worktree") FORCE-DELETE a peer session's unmerged commits — reproduced and pinned. `default_run_id()` also gains a pid suffix: it was second-granular, so two sessions starting in the same second got the same id and re-opened the collision through the namespace itself. `--run` is optional and omitting it reproduces the legacy layout byte-for-byte, so worktrees/branches cut by an older condukt are never orphaned or re-targeted. New e2e suite `worktree_namespace_concurrency.rs` observes both DoD conditions (both runs create; neither deletes the peer's ref) plus run-id distinctness and the legacy-layout pin. v0.7.87: cargo fmt --all reformatting only (fixes the 'build & commit plugin binaries' smoke workflow's `cargo fmt --all --check` gate, chronically red on main since 2026-07-21 per scripts/check-ci-red.py); no behavior change. v0.7.86: fixes 3 readdir/read-to-string fail-open swallows found in the workspace-wide fail-open audit — `state::all_runs` and `state::active_worktree_for_path` (readdir-flatten-swallow, `crates/condukt/src/state.rs`) and `diffrisk_record::worktree_rust_sources` no longer silently fold an unreadable directory/entry/file into "nothing here"; a genuinely-absent directory still degrades silently (legitimate), but any other IO error is now surfaced via `eprintln!` while the functions keep their existing fail-soft return contracts (`Vec<RunState>`/`Option<PathBuf>`) since both are documented as intentionally best-effort and `active_worktree_for_path` is not yet wired into any gate. New regression tests cover an unreadable project/run dir (chmod 000) and an absent run dir. v0.7.85: the four blastguard diff-risk consumption sites now resolve an `Undetermined` sensitive-path classification to the RESTRICTED side instead of reading it as "not sensitive": gate_exec degrades to Escalate (exit 1, human stop preserved), schedule force-gates and names the offending glob, review_brief treats every touched file as sensitive while emitting a driver line that distinguishes "the check could not run" from a measured hit, and diffrisk_record records under its own `diffrisk-undetermined` rule id rather than dropping the finding as non-High. v0.7.75: fix the runtime-conflict cleanup gap (design 625aa170 finding #1) — a task's branch landing now marks its `ActualChangeset` merged via a new `worktree::finalize_landed_branch` (calling overwatch's branch-keyed `store::mark_branch_merged`) wired into BOTH `merge()`'s clean-merge path AND `resolve_merge()`'s reconciled outcomes, so a cleanly-landed task no longer leaves `merged=false` within the lease TTL and spuriously HOLDS the next sequential task that touches a common file; also clears any stale `RuntimeOverlap` hold for the landed branch name and opportunistically prunes the cross-run changeset registry (bounded). Fixes the broken `run_pr` Poll remediation hint (`resolve-merge --branch` → the correct `--id`). New regression tests pin the pre-merge hold gate and the landed-peer cleanup. v0.7.74: runtime conflict detection + consensus merge-conflict resolution (design 625aa170). A mid-flight actual-diff overlap between two in-flight worktrees now HOLDS the second task's merge for review (routed into the SAME consensus review surface as a real merge conflict) rather than silently degrading to last-writer-wins; `worktree::merge` returns `MergeOutcome {Merged, Held(id), Conflict(id)}` (a HOLD/conflict is a hold-for-review, exit 0, not a hard error) and, on a real 3-way conflict, captures a `MergeConflictEntry` (conflicted files + both byte-bounded diffs) to the overwatch review surface. New reconciliation driver `condukt worktree resolve-merge --id <id>` applies a RECORDED resolution (Ours→`merge -s ours`, Theirs→`merge -X theirs`, Manual→materialize markers for a human) and completes the merge. Policy half (decision B): `policy::decide_conflict_resolution` (exposed via `policy decide|answer --conflict`) clamps an otherwise-`auto` verdict up to `escalate` — a conflict/overlap may ONLY escalate or block, NEVER auto-pick-a-side. v0.7.71: `schedule()` now warns (does not reject) when a task's `touched_files` entry looks like an absolute path (`/`-rooted or a Windows drive letter) or contains a `..` traversal component — such entries silently defeat the string-based conflict-detection heuristics documented as `normalize_entry`'s deliberate repo-relative-only scope. Warn (not reject) was chosen because `schedule()` is the decomposition-wide deterministic gate and a hard error there would stop the whole run over what is usually a false-positive-prone heuristic, not a certain conflict. Also adds a real end-to-end capstone test (`schedule_conflict_capstone_e2e.rs`) driving `schedule()` itself with a genuinely-overlapping pair, a normalize_entry-only-overlapping pair, and a genuinely-independent pair, asserting the first two serialize and the third stays parallel with no data loss; and `fugu_router_record_e2e.rs`, confirming the v0.7.66 `suggested_model`/`route_basis`/`tokens_input`/`tokens_output` wiring actually lands those fields in a real `episodes.jsonl` end-to-end. v0.7.70: `schedule::entries_conflict` now normalizes each touched-file entry (strip a leading `./`, collapse repeated `/`) before comparing, closing a false-negative gap where two different spellings of the identical path (e.g. `./src/a.rs` vs `src/a.rs`, or `src//a.rs` vs `src/a.rs`) went undetected as a conflict and could schedule two workers onto the same file in parallel. Audited for false positives too: confirmed (and pinned with a regression test) that disjoint globs sharing only a parent directory (`src/foo/*.rs` vs `src/bar/*.rs`) do NOT over-serialize, and that the literal-prefix-nesting heuristic's known conservative-but-safe over-approximation (e.g. `src/*.rs` vs `src/sub/*.rs`) is unchanged and intentional per this module's own "conservative: false conflict only serializes work (safe)" principle. v0.7.69: new `crates/condukt/tests/run_lock_concurrency.rs` spawns two real `condukt state claim-task` processes racing the SAME hashkey from different runs across 8 trials and asserts exactly one wins (with content-level assertions on the claimed/skipped JSON, not just exit codes, so a shared-tmp-file crash can never masquerade as a valid hard skip) — `RunLock` (ported from `backlog::lock`/`overwatch::lock`) had no dedicated multi-process regression test proving the port itself was correct end-to-end. `claim::claim_tasks` gains a test-only `CONDUKT_TEST_CLAIM_DELAY_MS`-gated `artificial_race_delay()` (mirrors `overwatch::lease::artificial_race_delay`) to deterministically widen the race window inside the `RunLock`-held critical section; no-op in production. v0.7.68: `orphans()` (worktree.rs) no longer misreports another repo's live worktree as condukt debris when `worktree_base` is shared across multiple, unrelated git repositories on the same machine — a candidate directory is now only flagged as an orphan if its `.git` (file pointer for a linked worktree, or dir for a plain clone) actually resolves under `repo`'s own `.git` common dir AND isn't in `repo`'s registered worktree list; a directory owned by a different repo is silently skipped, while a directory with no `.git` at all is still conservatively treated as orphan (unchanged). New regression tests `orphans_ignores_other_repos_worktree` and `orphans_detects_stale_worktree_of_own_repo` cover the new behavior and the real-world stale-worktree case this fix must not regress. v0.7.67: `record_runs` now checks the actual exit status of the `fugu-router record` subprocess instead of only catching a spawn `Err`, so a non-zero exit (e.g. a stale PATH-shadowed `fugu-router` binary rejecting a flag) is no longer silently counted as a successful record; also resolves `fugu-router`'s binary path via `~/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json`'s plugin-cache `installPath` first, falling back to the bare command name only if resolution fails, so a stale `~/.cargo/bin/fugu-router` can no longer shadow the correct plugin-installed version. v0.7.66: `TaskState`/`state set` gain measurement-only `route_basis`/`route_confidence`/`route_rationale` (the routing `Decision`'s provenance from `route.json`) and `lines_added`/`lines_removed` (measured `git diff --stat` insertions/deletions), plus a new `state::resolve_agent_tokens` (mirrors `resolve_agent_cost`, exact agent-id match against `gauge subagents --json`'s new `tokens_input`/`tokens_output`); `record_runs` threads all of these through to `fugu-router record`'s matching new flags so routing decisions and task cost/size can be retrospectively correlated against actual pass/fail outcomes. None of it is consulted by condukt's own scheduling/routing — purely additive, backward-compatible. Deterministic orchestration engine for Claude Code: an interpreter/worker/verifier skill plus a Rust binary that schedules tasks into parallel/serial batches by file-conflict analysis, manages the git-worktree lifecycle, tracks run state, and gates completion. v0.7.65: fixes a near-total cost-recording failure — `gauge subagents` cost lookup previously matched on a Task description prefix (`"<task-id>: "`) that real-world worker descriptions almost never honored, so `cost_usd` silently recorded as `0.0` (0/66 haiku+opus and 4/142 sonnet episodes ever got a nonzero cost). `state set --agent-id` now stores the Task tool's exact `agentId` on `TaskState`/`RecordSpec`; `record_runs` resolves cost via exact agent-id match against `gauge subagents --json` (`state::resolve_agent_cost`, built on a pure/testable `parse_agent_cost` core), falling back to the manually recorded `--cost` when unresolved. SKILL.md Phase 5/6 make `--agent-id` the primary path. v0.7.64: wires the `adversarial` panel (decided in v0.7.4x-era `adversarial.rs`) into Phase 6 of the SKILL — `condukt adversarial plan` gates whether a completion (GATE-crate change or global switch) gets an N-skeptic refutation panel instead of a single verifier; adds `verify::resolve_skeptic_model`/`condukt state skeptic-model` to spread panel members across model tiers excluding the worker's own (never collapses onto a shared blind spot). Non-engaging tasks run the existing single-verifier path unchanged. v0.7.63: opt-in **shadow-run** mode — `shadow-run enable|disable|status` (default disabled) plus `exec`/`finish` run the SAME task under a second model in an independent worktree (reusing existing worktree create/discard) to produce a clean pass/fail/cost/duration comparison for `fugu-router record --class shadow-run`; the shadow worktree is ALWAYS discarded, never merged. Manual-trigger only — no API/hook input exposes remaining rate-limit-window time, so no automatic firing is implemented. v0.7.62: task-duration measurement — `TaskState` gains `started_at` (set when a task transitions to `running`); `records_for_run` computes `duration_secs` from `(started_at, updated_at)` and `record_runs()` passes it to `fugu-router record --duration`, populating the new measurement-only `Episode.duration_secs` field (routing/scoring logic in fugu-router's `policy.rs` is unchanged). v0.7.61: `verify::mechanical_cmd` now tokenizes command strings (mechanical_check hint + backtick-extracted done_criteria command) via a new quote/escape-aware `parse_argv` (shlex-backed) instead of `split_whitespace`, so a quoted argument containing a space survives as one argv token; falls back to `split_whitespace` on unparseable input. v0.7.60: `verify::run_check` now gates each declared check command through blastguard's pure detector (same `detect("Bash", ...)` call already used by `launch_and_reflux`) before spawning `sh -c`; a flagged command is refused fail-closed and reported as a non-passing `CheckResult` (exit -1) instead of being executed. New test `run_check_blocks_destructive_command_via_blastguard` proves a `rm -rf /` check never reaches the shell. v0.7.59: gatelog.rs's `append_decision`, `append_circuit`, and `append_gate_exec` now use harness-core's `append::append_line()` (single write_all syscall) instead of `writeln!` (body+newline as two syscalls), preventing interleaving of concurrent JSONL records under O_APPEND. Regression test `concurrent_decision_appends_never_interleave` ensures 8 threads appending 100 records each produce parseable lines (all 800 survive, none concatenated). v0.7.58: audited `lessons.rs`'s `harvest()` (production JSON-facts path) — already fail-soft throughout (`.ok()`/`.and_then()`/`.unwrap_or()`), no raw `.unwrap()`/`.expect()`; the flagged calls were inside `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` only. Also fixed a real test flake found while confirming green under parallel execution: a lessons.rs test mutating the process-global `LESSONS_STORE_DIR` env var now serializes via its own `ENV_LOCK` mutex (mirrors the existing `replan.rs` precedent). v0.7.57: `worktree.rs`'s git subprocess calls are now bounded by a 45s timeout (wait_timeout + process-group kill) instead of a plain unbounded `Command::output()`, so a hung `git` can no longer wedge a condukt run indefinitely; `create()`'s "worktree must be outside the repo" check now canonicalizes the candidate worktree path before comparing against the canonical repo root, closing a TOCTOU-adjacent bypass via a non-canonical `worktree_base`. v0.7.56: `verify::tests::skip_eligible_without_command_fails_soft` no longer relies on a `panic!` inside the invariant-violating runner closure — it records the invocation via a flag, logs it, and asserts the flag stays false, so the test path never aborts the process (production `mechanical_skip_verdict` behavior unchanged). v0.7.55: docs-only — SKILL.md Phase 7 documents the `state reconcile` exit 2 (duplicate_completion) escalation branch. v0.7.54: `gate_exec`'s escalate-finding call site follows overwatch's extended `record_finding`/`ReviewFinding.rationale` signature (no behavior change). Subscription-native (skill + agents + hook, no API key).

plugins.name: context-governor
plugins.description: A thin control layer around Claude Code's built-in compaction: pin + lossless-recall + retrieval + tool-hygiene, wired as a single hook-dispatch binary. Separates the three axes it touches — size (window occupancy), cost (recompute/cache), correctness (norm preservation) — and never writes its own lossy summarizer (compression is delegated to built-in compaction). Subscription-native (hooks + binary, no API key).

plugins.name: ctxrot
plugins.description: v0.5.21: `bin/ctxrot` (the POSIX launcher) no longer maps a MISSING per-platform binary to a blanket silent `exit 0`. A missing build means the check did not run, and exit-0-with-no-output is byte-identical to a clean run, so every verdict-bearing subcommand silently read as "nothing to flag": preguard granted the load gate, toolguard let an unmeasured payload through, stop ended the turn as if the budget check had passed, and statusline rendered the blank bar that reads as headroom (the 3b1eb24 fail-open). Each now resolves the cannot-determine on the restrictive side of its OWN protocol — preguard emits `permissionDecision: ask` (a refusal to guess; a `deny` would be unescapable for every Read/Bash), toolguard emits an `additionalContext` UNMEASURED marker, stop emits `{"decision":"block"}` bounded by `stop_hook_active` exactly like harness_core::gate::run's panic barrier (empty stdin = a manual run: exit 1, no fabricated decision), and statusline prints the explicit `unknown` band. The CLI/skill-consumed subcommands (note/metrics/ctx/usage/eval/…), whose empty stdout would be read as real data ("no notes", "nothing dropped"), now exit 1 like bin/evalkit. Only the pure-observability hooks (guard/rescue/restore/distill-bg — conditional prose injected into context, no machine consumer) keep exit 0, and they still report on stderr; README.ja.md gains the launcher classification table enumerating each subcommand's downstream consumers (CLAUDE.md §1's requirement for any module claiming the non-verdict carve-out) and states the residual limit that hook stderr is only visible in debug output. src/main.rs's stale "on any error we exit 0 and stay silent" module docstring was corrected to match the code. New tests/launcher_missing_binary.rs pins every row of that table, plus that a PRESENT binary is still exec'd with args passed through. v0.5.18: `hooks::stop::run()` now returns `(json, check_kind: &'static str)`; `stop_run` records an `overwatch` `ViolationSource::Ctxrot` event via a new `emit_violation(root, session, check_kind)` (observed check_kind values: `unmeasurable-transcript`, `budget-threshold-crossed`), feeding the unified review-queue. v0.5.16: cargo fmt --all reformatting only (fixes the 'build & commit plugin binaries' smoke workflow's `cargo fmt --all --check` gate, chronically red on main since 2026-07-21 per scripts/check-ci-red.py); no behavior change. Context-rot guard for Claude Code: detect, rescue, restore, distill, and CONTROL what loads into context (rule-based allow/deny gate + /ctx pin/drop/load + switchable carryover). Subscription-native (hooks + subagent + skill, no API key). v0.5.15: `usage::find_transcript_for_session`'s `~/.claude/projects` scan no longer swallows a permission-denied (or other non-NotFound) read_dir/entry error into the same silent `None` as a legitimately-absent directory — the non-NotFound case now also surfaces via `eprintln!`; the `None` → "unknown" readout callers already render is unchanged (an absent dir was never a fail-open here, since the caller already treats `None` as cannot-determine). New regression tests cover an absent projects dir and a chmod-000 unreadable one. v0.5.14: the Stop hook now runs under harness-core's `run_guarded` panic barrier — a panic in `stop_run` fails CLOSED (`decision:block`) instead of the old `run_hook` behavior of silently exiting 0 with no decision. v0.5.12: the Stop-hook compact nudge now fails CLOSED on a cannot-determine reading — when `estimate_tokens` falls back to the cache-blind bytes proxy (no `usage` block parsed) yet that proxy, a LOWER bound on true usage, has already reached band 1, the hook surfaces a one-shot `/compact` nudge instead of silently allowing a possibly-over-budget session to keep growing; previously its high 0.90 block threshold let a truncated/corrupt transcript read low and never nudge (behavioral twin of the v0.5.10/v0.5.11 render fixes). Bounded to fire ONCE per session (dedicated `.compact-unmeasured` sentinel, never a turn-trap); a genuine early session below band 1 stays silent (no over-alarm) and the eventual genuine over-threshold reading still blocks. v0.5.11: the context-usage readout (statusline + `ctxrot usage`) no longer renders a bytes-proxy estimate as a confident band — `estimate_tokens`'s source (`"bytes"` = a rough size/4 guess with no real usage block, vs `"usage"` = authoritative) is threaded through `usage::line` instead of discarded, so an estimate carries an `est?` marker and, when it lands in the green band, is DIMMED (neutral, not confident green) so a truncated/corrupt transcript reading low can't read as "plenty of headroom"; a high estimate keeps its alarming color and authoritative readings are unchanged. v0.5.10: the `statusline` render now fails CLOSED on a cannot-determine — a non-empty-but-unparseable payload, or a transcript that can't be read/estimated, renders an explicit non-green `?% … unknown` band (mirroring `ctxrot usage`'s "不明") instead of printing nothing; a blank status bar silently read as "plenty of headroom" (fail-open twin of the already-hardened Stop-hook path). Empty stdin / no session still renders blank; exit stays 0 so the bar never crashes. v0.5.9: the preguard (PreToolUse) and toolguard (PostToolUse) hooks now wrap their detectors in a `std::panic::catch_unwind` barrier (`analyse`) — a panic in the analysis maps to a deny (preguard) or a fail-closed placeholder+nudge (toolguard) instead of the un-analysed call/output silently passing through, closing a fail-open (blastguard 同型). v0.5.8: `guard::fetch_session_lease`'s `overwatch lease` subprocess call is now bounded by an 8s timeout (wait_timeout, kill+reap on expiry) instead of a plain unbounded `Command::output()`, so a hung overwatch binary can no longer wedge the UserPromptSubmit hook; the spawn/timeout/kill mechanics are split into a testable `run_with_timeout` helper.

plugins.name: curate
plugins.description: Promote fugu-router playbooks into versioned golden eval datasets for evalkit: turn the append-only routing log into a curated, deduplicated holdout set. Mechanical acceptance criteria (`cargo test`, a backticked command) become runnable golden cases; the rest become drafts for a human to fill. The supply side of the offline eval loop. plugins.name: deepwiki
plugins.description: v0.1.5: cargo fmt --all reformatting only (fixes the 'build & commit plugin binaries' smoke workflow's `cargo fmt --all --check` gate, chronically red on main since 2026-07-21 per scripts/check-ci-red.py); no behavior change. Repository architecture wiki for Claude Code: a /deepwiki command that maps the repo with a bundled Rust scanner, has a subagent write & refresh hierarchical wiki pages (.deepwiki/*.md) with source links, and tracks freshness against git. Inspired by Devin Wiki. Subscription-native (binary + subagent + command, no API key). v0.1.4: `scan.rs`'s three readdir walks (`scan`'s top-level summary, `walk`, `count_files`) no longer swallow an unreadable subdirectory or entry via `.flatten()`/`let-else` into the same silent skip as a legitimately-vanished one — a non-NotFound error now surfaces via `eprintln!` while the scan still degrades to whatever was readable (this is a best-effort repo-map generator feeding a wiki-writer subagent, not a gate, so partial results remain correct behavior — only the silent swallowing of a real permission error was the bug). New regression test scans a tree with a chmod-000 subdirectory and confirms the readable files are still counted.

plugins.name: difflog
plugins.description: Session diff-log for Claude Code: snapshot HEAD at SessionStart, write a structured git diff summary (commits, stat, files changed, bounded diff body) at SessionEnd. A /difflog skill can generate a human-readable narrative from the log. Subscription-native (no API key). v0.1.5: `list`/`last`'s shared `md_entries` helper no longer swallows an unreadable individual directory entry via `.filter_map(|e| e.ok())`, and distinguishes a missing `log_dir` ("not found") from an existing-but-unreadable one ("unreadable", now surfaced) instead of both silently reading as "no logs". New regression tests cover an absent dir, a chmod-000 unreadable dir, and md-only filtering.

plugins.name: ship
plugins.description: v0.1.9: cargo fmt --all reformatting only (fixes the 'build & commit plugin binaries' smoke workflow's `cargo fmt --all --check` gate, chronically red on main since 2026-07-21 per scripts/check-ci-red.py); no behavior change. Shipping-ritual nudge for Claude Code: deterministically detect unshipped state (uncommitted changes, unmerged condukt/* branches, leftover worktrees, unpushed commits, stale plugin binaries) and remind you to commit・merge・push・rebuild・rollout. A /ship skill and a fail-soft SessionEnd hook surface the checklist; only the plugin-rebuild (`--run-safe`, now `--stage-repo` so it refreshes the committed binary that stale-detection measures) and plugin-rollout (`ship rollout`, automates `/plugin update`) steps are auto-runnable — commit/merge/push stay human-gated. Subscription-native (no API key).

plugins.name: donegate
plugins.description: v0.1.21: re-bless the verdict compile-fail trybuild golden stderr again — CI's `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable` has no `rust-src` component, which changes how rustc renders `note:` snippets pointing into std/core; a local toolchain with rust-src installed produces the longer form and silently re-diverges the golden. Reproduced against a `--profile minimal` toolchain matching CI exactly. No contract change. v0.1.20: re-bless the verdict compile-fail trybuild golden stderr again (rustc now emits additional note-body lines for E0599; the compile-fail invariant is unchanged, same category of drift as v0.1.18). v0.1.18: re-bless the verdict trybuild .stderr (removed stale std-lib note bodies that a newer rustc no longer renders; the compile-fail invariant is unchanged). v0.1.17: new `emit_violations(root, session, failing: &[String])` records one `overwatch` `ViolationSource::Donegate` event per failing check name (fmt/clippy/test) after `gate_run` blocks a Stop, feeding the unified review-queue. Completion-verification gate for Claude Code: on Stop, run your acceptance commands as subprocesses and block the stop until every required check is green, feeding failures back for an auto-fix loop. Subscription-native (one hook + bundled Rust binary, no API key). v0.1.8: added #![deny(clippy::panic)] at crate root.

plugins.name: evalkit
plugins.description: Offline golden-regression eval harness for Claude Code plugins: read golden *.jsonl cases (file-content or CLI-output assertions) and exit non-zero when a prompt edit or CLI contract regresses. The offline sibling of condukt's online verifier — runnable as a CI gate with no API key. Subscription-native (one bundled Rust binary).

plugins.name: benchkit
plugins.description: v0.1.8: `auditsample.rs`'s `gate_name()` match arm now covers the 6 new `ViolationSource` variants (Donegate/Reviewgate/Tdd/Budgetguard/Autoflow/Ctxrot) added to overwatch's cross-gate ledger; no behavior change to sampling logic. External-benchmark (SWE-bench Verified) runner for Claude Code plugins: a typed SWE-bench Instance model, a deterministic fixture-based JSONL loader, and a gated `download` subcommand that shells out to `curl` (no HTTP crate) to fetch the Princeton NLP dataset only on explicit invocation. Subscription-native (one bundled Rust binary).

plugins.name: flow
plugins.description: Unified source→executor driver for Claude Code: a /flow skill that binds the task SOURCES (compass next-move + backlog queue) to the EXECUTOR (condukt, model-routed by fugu-router) in one HOTL loop — gate on compass freshness, pick the highest-priority task, hand it to condukt, verify, mark done, repeat. A SessionStart hook proposes /flow every session when open work exists (propose-then-confirm). Subscription-native (skill + hook + bundled Rust binary, no API key). v0.1.12: Step 3-2 now documents a default fork-wrapping bias for /condukt invocations (exception: xs-class single-file tasks where the user wants interactive visibility) and a manual `fugu-router record --delegation fork|inline` logging convention, feeding a new open hypothesis measuring fork-vs-inline cost/duration. v0.1.13: the manual delegation-recording convention now includes a self-check step — after `fugu-router record --delegation`, call `fugu-router audit-recent --class flow-delegation --within <secs>` and retry/warn on a miss, instead of trusting the record call landed. v0.1.14: Step 3-4's per-cycle heartbeat now also refreshes the backlog lock itself (`backlog lock heartbeat --session-id <id>`), not just the condukt claim registry — closing a gap where a long-running loop could lose its cross-session backlog lock to a stale-TTL reap even though it was still actively working (fail-soft if `backlog` is absent/fails). v0.2.1: Step 3-3's backlog add convention now also references docs/backlog-tag-taxonomy.md for cross-project work-category tags.

plugins.name: fugu-router
plugins.description: v0.1.25: `Episode.duration_secs` is now tri-state (`Option<f64>`) — an absent field OR a legacy on-disk `0.0` both deserialize to `None` ("unmeasured"), never conflated with a genuine measured zero, via a custom `de_duration_secs` deserializer; a new writer omits the field entirely when unmeasured (`skip_serializing_if`). `record --duration` is now `Option<f64>`: a non-positive value (0 or negative) is an explicit error + non-zero exit ("omit --duration to record the episode as unmeasured"), never silently stored. `stats` and `duration`/`duration-outliers` surface a duration-coverage count (`measured_n/total_n`, plus `duration_coverage` in `--json`) so the fraction of episodes with a real measurement is visible instead of a silent 0.0-average dilution; `duration-outliers` and `delegation-stats` now average only measured episodes. RED→GREEN recorded via tdd --task t3. v0.1.24: new mode axis `--mode fast|normal|high` for `route`/`suggest` — a deterministic clamp applied AFTER the policy has already picked a worker/verifier pair (never touches `decide`/`decide_bandit`'s learning logic). `fast` shifts the worker one tier down (capped at sonnet — opus never selected as worker or verifier); `high` shifts one tier up (capped at opus); `normal` is the backward-compatible identity default. The verifier is always recomputed from the clamped worker via `policy::verifier_model`, additionally capped at sonnet under `fast`. Precedence: `--mode` flag > env `FUGU_ROUTER_MODE` > config.toml `mode` > `normal`; an invalid env/config value is an explicit error + non-zero exit, never silently coerced to `normal`. A `gated` decision is a no-op under every mode. Ordering: the mode clamp runs BEFORE `downgrade_for_budget` — budget wins over a mode preference, and the rationale records both the mode's shift and any budget negation so a `high` pick never silently disappears. `Episode` gains a measurement-only `mode: Option<String>` field (`record --mode`); an absent value means "not recorded", never conflated with `Some("normal")`. v0.1.22: `fingerprint::collect_skills`'s SKILL.md corpus walk no longer silently skips an unreadable directory/entry/file the same way it skips a legitimately-absent one — since this module exists specifically to detect a silent skill edit, a SKILL.md that becomes unreadable defeating that detection is now surfaced via `eprintln!` while the walk still degrades to whatever was readable (fail-soft, unchanged contract). New regression test: a chmod-000 subdirectory doesn't panic and the still-readable sibling SKILL.md is still hashed. v0.1.20: new `duration-outliers [--json] [--threshold <x>]` command flags models whose avg duration within a task class is a relative outlier vs other models in the same class (default threshold 1.5x the cross-model mean), and cross-references outlier-vs-normal effective pass rate — the measurement tool built to test PDO hypothesis ae64db03. v0.1.19: `Episode` gains measurement-only `route_basis`/`route_confidence`/`route_rationale` (the routing `Decision`'s provenance), `lines_added`/`lines_removed`, and `tokens_input`/`tokens_output`, all `Option<_>` and backward-compatible; `record` gains matching `--route-basis`/`--route-confidence`/`--route-rationale`/`--lines-added`/`--lines-removed`/`--tokens-input`/`--tokens-output` flags. Not consulted by `policy::route`/`decide_bandit` — exists so routing decisions and task cost can be retrospectively correlated against actual pass/fail outcomes. fugu-style per-model routing for Claude Code orchestration. Learns from past task outcomes (which model passed verification, at what cost) and picks the cheapest Claude tier that historically clears similar work. Feeds condukt's suggested_model deterministically; records outcomes back to a local episode store. No API key, no embedding service — lexical k-NN over a JSONL store. v0.1.13: every git subprocess in `cmd_sync` (pull/clone/status/add/diff/commit/push) is now bounded by a timeout (30s network ops, 10s local ops) via `wait-timeout`, killing a hung/stalled git process instead of wedging the sync command indefinitely. v0.1.12: `store::append_playbook` now writes body+newline in one `write_all` call (mirroring `append`'s existing single-syscall pattern) instead of `writeln!`'s two syscalls, closing the same O_APPEND interleaving hazard for playbook records; a JSON-serialization failure now propagates as an `io::Result` error instead of silently writing an empty line. New regression test `concurrent_append_playbook_never_interleaves_records`. v0.1.14: `Episode` gains a measurement-only `duration_secs: f64` field (`#[serde(default)]`, backward-compatible with older JSONL lines) and `record` gains a `--duration` flag threading it through; not consulted by `policy::route`/`decide_bandit` — routing/scoring behavior is unchanged. v0.1.15: `Episode` gains a measurement-only `delegation: Option<String>` field (`#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if)]`, backward-compatible) and `record` gains an optional `--delegation <fork|inline>` flag, for manually comparing /flow's condukt-invocation delegation strategy; not consulted by `policy::route`/`decide_bandit`. v0.1.16: docs-only — README/README.ja and the spec draft now document the `--duration`/`--delegation` record flags that shipped in v0.1.14/v0.1.15 but were missing from user-facing docs. v0.1.17: adds `audit-recent --class <c> --within <secs>`, a self-check subcommand (exit 0 if an episode of that class was recorded within the window, 1 if not) so a caller like /flow's delegation-recording step can verify its own `record` call actually landed instead of trusting a self-report. v0.1.18: adds `delegation-stats [--json]`, comparing fork vs inline flow-delegation episodes (count/pass-rate/avg cost/avg duration, delegation value normalized for case/whitespace).

plugins.name: gauge
plugins.description: Local LLMOps telemetry for Claude Code: a Stop hook that reads each session's transcript and records token usage, cache hits, tool calls, latency, and estimated cost to a local store — then `gauge report` rolls it up by project, model, and day. v0.3.11: `find_transcript`'s `~/.claude/projects` scan no longer swallows a permission-denied (or other non-NotFound) read_dir/entry/metadata error into the same silent `None`/skip as a legitimately-absent path — now surfaced via `eprintln!`, closing a gap that could otherwise hide a real transcript from cost/usage reporting; a missing projects dir still legitimately yields `None`. New regression tests cover an absent dir, a chmod-000 unreadable dir, and picking the most-recently-modified transcript. v0.3.7 adds a manually-registered rate-limit window (`gauge config set-window --hours <f64> --last-reset <ISO8601>` / `config show`), letting other tools query an approximate reset ETA — fail-soft, no automatic detection. v0.3.8: docs-only — README/README.ja and the spec draft now document the v0.3.7 `config set-window`/`config show` subcommands. v0.3.9: `gauge subagents --json` now also emits `tokens_input`/`tokens_output` per sub-agent, so callers can record real token usage alongside cost. Observability for your own agent runs, subscription-native (one hook + bundled Rust binary, no API key, nothing leaves the machine).

Unified HOTL status dashboard for Claude Code. A /status command runs a bundled Rust binary that aggregates budgetguard's spend ledger, gauge's session records (recent sessions + cost), and taskprog's progress file into one human-on-the-loop view. Subscription-native (binary + command, no API key). A lightweight SessionStart hook additionally warns (fail-soft, silent when healthy) if a registered hook's binary is missing from disk, or if a stray PATH binary (e.g. a stale ~/.cargo/bin copy) shadows a newer plugin-cache copy.

plugins.name: precommit-audit
plugins.description: v0.1.13: fixed the gitleaks check (backlog 848913b8) — it was passing `--source ctx.root` (the whole working tree) under `--no-git`, so .gitignore'd build artifacts (e.g. Python __pycache__/*.pyc, which fold source string literals into compiled constants) could false-positive on secret-shaped test fixtures and repeatedly block unrelated commits. It now copies only the actually-changed files (ctx.files) into a scratch dir and scans that, matching the doc comment's original (previously false) claim. v0.1.12: closed the recorded gap — .githooks/pre-commit now has scripts/check-hardcoded-secret.py (secret-guard), an independent stdlib-only python3 gate over added lines matching check_hardcoded_secret's key/shape rules (backlog aa74be67); precommit-audit itself is still not wholesale-integrated into that hook (unchanged self-apply decision). v0.1.11: documented this repo's own self-apply positioning — precommit-audit is not wired into .githooks/pre-commit (the repo's own git-commit-time gate) but does fire as a Stop hook here via user-scope install; recorded the gap that .githooks/pre-commit has no hardcoded-secret-scan equivalent. v0.1.9: closed a fail-open where a panic mid-audit was swallowed into exit(0) — a clean/allow verdict — so any crash reported the working set it had just FAILED to scan as clean (99b71596, blastguard#3 twin). A caught panic now exits with the mode's BLOCKING code (stop→2, precommit→1), consistent with the git-error and incomplete-scan paths that already fail closed; under SessionEnd a non-zero exit surfaces as a failed hook rather than a silent pass. Config-driven pre-commit static audit for Claude Code: a Stop hook that runs generic checks plus your project rules (from a TOML file) over the pending diff — shelling out to git and optional linters — and blocks the stop, feeding findings back to the agent until they're clean. Subscription-native (one hook + bundled Rust binary, no API key).

plugins.name: reviewgate
plugins.description: v0.1.17: the reviewgate-typing subagent reviews for whether type checking and determinism are actually used — five passes (prose/signature/call-site/body/early-return), a has-a-verdict gate that requires enumerating downstream consumers before reporting, and a mirror check that treats a correct tri-state twin as evidence its sibling is a migration miss. v0.1.16: new `emit_violation(root, session, tag)` records an `overwatch` `ViolationSource::Reviewgate` event tagged with the block reason after `review_run` blocks a Stop, feeding the unified review-queue. Code-review gate for Claude Code: on Stop, review the diff before the agent can declare done. In inject mode it blocks the stop and injects a review rubric so the running agent self-reviews (no API key); in subprocess mode it runs an independent reviewer and surfaces only its findings. Subscription-native, bundled Rust binary. v0.1.10: added #![deny(clippy::panic)] at crate root (existing test-module panic!() calls allowed locally).

plugins.name: specguard
plugins.description: v0.2.48: specforge ratify now has an EXIT to the queue — it files one backlog item per requirement of the spec it just ratified (src/forge/queue.rs, DESIGN.md §5.4). Before this a ratified spec had no implemented path into the queue at all; the only spec→backlog handoff was prose telling a human to run `backlog add` by hand, so specforge could produce canon but not work. Each item carries the spec id, the requirement id, and the requirement's acceptance criteria VERBATIM as its done_criteria block, so condukt's interpreter lifts them instead of re-deriving them from the statement (re-derivation is where a requirement quietly loses its teeth). Idempotent via a `req:<spec id>:<req id>` identity tag derived from the two ids alone: re-ratifying adds zero, editing a statement does not orphan its item into a duplicate, and another spec's R0 does not collide with this one's. The listing passes no --status filter on purpose (measured: `backlog list` still returns done tasks), so a COMPLETED requirement keeps suppressing its own re-queue rather than being resurrected. Cannot-determine does not guess (CLAUDE.md §3): a missing `backlog` binary, a non-zero exit, or an unparseable listing resolves to neither "queue is empty" (which duplicates everything) nor "already queued" (which silently discards what a human ratified) — it exits 9 (EXIT_QUEUE_FAILED) with the ratification intact, and `specforge queue --id <id>` retries the handoff alone. `specforge queue` refuses an unratified spec with exit 6 (the queue is downstream of consent) and `ratify --no-queue` makes opting out explicit rather than silent. v0.2.36: closed fail-open #7 (61599e06) — an audit whose marker was present but whose `needs_user` verdict was absent/empty/unrecognised was parsed as `no`/clean, advancing the baseline over content whose verdict was never established. parse.rs now fails closed with an asymmetric rule: the SURFACE side is liberal (a `yes`-prefixed token is a finding) but the CLEAN side is strict — only the bare token `no` clears the audit (the old `starts_with("no")` also cleared "not sure"/"no idea"/"not comparable", natural cannot-determine phrasings). Anything else is a first-class `indeterminate` state → needs_user=true that stays STICKY through the verify/refute pass (a skeptic can't drop it back to clean). All three audit prompts (audit/decisions/completeness) fixed in lockstep to instruct the auditor to emit `yes` (not `no`) when it cannot compare, and to emit exactly `yes` or `no`. 仕様↔実装 整合監査ハーネスを Claude Code から subscription-native に実行する。各 shard を read-only な in-session subagent で監査し (nested claude --print なし)、決定的ハーネス (scope/render/parse/report) は specguard バイナリに委譲する。

plugins.name: stuckguard
plugins.description: v0.1.25: verdict-monotonicity の proptest を追加した（backlog a7d41587、テストのみ・production の挙動は不変）。永続化されたセッション履歴を truncate / corrupt / empty / chmod 000 しても「詰まっていない」へ倒れないことを性質として固定する。この経路は既に fail-closed（`main::watch` は Undetermined な load を nudge に解決する）なので修正ではなく ratchet であり、将来 `SessionState::default()` を静かに戻す編集をその編集について書かれていないテストが捕まえる。通ること自体は証拠にならないので、fail-closed 側を剥がした版を同一ファイル内に置いて性質が実際に落ちることを示す mutation テストと、4 種の degradation が全て実際に効いていることを確認する coverage テストを併置した（no-op になった degradation が黙って skip され続けるのを防ぐ）。 Stuck-loop detector + escalation for Claude Code: a PostToolUse hook that spots repeated identical actions and edit thrash, then injects an escalating nudge to change approach or ask the user for help. Subscription-native (one hook + bundled Rust binary, no API key).

plugins.name: taskprog
