plugins.name: tdd
plugins.description: v0.1.21: new `emit_violation(root, session, check_kind)` records an `overwatch` `ViolationSource::Tdd` event when the gate blocks a Stop for missing test coverage, feeding the unified review-queue. Test-first gate for Claude Code: a Stop hook that blocks the turn when implementation code lands without an accompanying test, plus a /tdd skill and red/green/verify subcommands that make test-first (RED before GREEN) a verifiable artifact. Subscription-native (one hook + skill + bundled Rust binary, no API key). v0.1.20: config.rs's local GATE_CRATES const is now `pub use harness_core::fleet::GATE_CRATES;`, removing a duplicate hand-written copy that had independently drifted (lost `overwatch`) in the past. v0.1.18: gate verdict now routes through harness_core::verdict (compass DoD1).

plugins.name: tracekit
plugins.description: Span-tree tracer for condukt runs: record one run's interpreter→worker→verifier phases as a parent-linked span tree (phase, model, ms, cost, status), render it with `tracekit trace <RID>`, and export OpenTelemetry GenAI-semconv JSON. Answers which phase of a failed run was slow/expensive/broke. Subscription-native (one bundled Rust binary, file-only, no network, no API key).

plugins.name: autoflow
plugins.description: v0.1.17: cannot-determine no longer resolves to "no work left" — `backlog::find_open`, `condukt::find_pending` and `find_backlog_binary` return `harness_core::verdict::Determination`, keeping "could not observe" apart from "observed empty". An unreadable/unparseable condukt run-state (one task missing `status` used to fail the whole document and hide healthy tasks with it), a `backlog list` that fails to spawn or exits non-zero, a queue answering in an unrecognised status vocabulary, and an unlistable plugin-cache dir are all `Undetermined`. `Phase::Done` — the latch that silences autoflow for the rest of a session — now requires an observed-empty queue; undetermined blocks visibly through `Verdict::stop_decision()` and leaves the phase untouched so the next Stop re-observes. An undetermined binary lookup also stands the auto-loop down rather than skipping the driver-liveness check and double-driving a live queue. v0.1.16: replaced the count-proxy stops with progress-based continuation (backlog 422d256a facets 822c7209/9aa0031f) — the condukt loop's auto-≤4×/ask-from-5× count split and the backlog loop's silent Phase::Done at max_backlog_prompts are removed; both now continue while the remaining-work set shrinks and escalate visibly (never silently) via a no-progress streak vs cfg.stuck_threshold (default 3), consulting condukt state autonomy-check for the escalation wording. v0.1.15: strengthened the Tier 2 delegation-record advisory's own regression test after an independent verifier found the prior fixture vacuous (it quoted both trigger substrings in one doc excerpt, so it passed against pre-fix logic too); rebuilt to the true false-positive shape and verified empirically against a reimplementation of the pre-fix logic. No functional code change. v0.1.14: Tier 2 delegation-record advisory fixed two false-positive classes (backlog d8051ed4) — it now matches only genuine executed Bash `tool_use` invocations (not raw transcript substring matches, which could fire on the `/flow` skill's own doc text quoting example commands) and scopes condukt run-completion checks to THIS session's own run id (extracted from its transcript) instead of the project-wide latest run file, which could belong to a concurrent unrelated session. v0.1.13: new `emit_violation(cwd, session, check_kind)` records an `overwatch` `ViolationSource::Autoflow` event for its Stop-hook blocking decisions, feeding the unified review-queue. Session-end auto-flow gate for Claude Code: on Stop, prompt /record once, then loop /condukt and /backlog while work keeps progressing (progress-based continuation, no call-count ceiling; stalled progress escalates visibly; stops only when the pending/open set is empty). Also fires a fail-soft Tier 2 advisory when a /flow-driven condukt run completes without any evidence of a fugu-router delegation record. Subscription-native (one hook + bundled Rust binary, no API key). v0.1.9: Stop hook now runs under harness-core's run_guarded panic barrier (fail-closed block on crash instead of silent allow).

plugins.name: hypothesis
plugins.description: v0.1.8: the store's load->mutate->save cycle is now protected by an exclusive file lock (`StoreLock`, ported from backlog::lock/condukt::lock::RunLock/overwatch::lock::LeaseLock) so two concurrent processes mutating the store (e.g. `validate`/`reject`/`confidence`) can no longer lose one update to a last-writer-wins race; a multi-process regression test proves the fix (and that it fails without the lock). PDO hypothesis lifecycle management for Claude Code: a /hypothesis skill plus create/validate/list/reject subcommands and a SessionStart hook to create, validate, and track discovery hypotheses aligned with compass goals. Subscription-native (skill + hook + bundled Rust binary, no API key).

plugins.name: overwatch
plugins.description: v0.2.16: 監査ラウンド台帳の読み取りを三値化した（backlog a7d41787 の verdict-monotonicity）。`store::read_audit_rounds` は不在の台帳だけを Known(空) とし、読めない・パースできない台帳は Undetermined に解決する（旧実装は `Err(_) => Ok(Vec::new())` と壊れた行の無言スキップ）。`converging` 自体も三値になり、window 内が 2 ラウンド未満なら `unknown` を返す（旧: vacuously true）。出荷済み 0.2.15 バイナリでは `audit_rounds.jsonl` を truncate / corrupt / chmod 000 するだけで `converging: false` → `true` が exit 0 で得られており、証拠を壊すほど判定が良くなる状態だった（実測）。`audit-metrics` と `audit-round close` は読み取り不能で abort する（close は全体書き戻しなので部分読みは記録の破壊になる）。新規 proptest `tests/verdict_monotonicity.rs` が harness-core の新 `degrade` モジュールを使ってこの単調性を性質として固定する。残存ギャップ（レコード境界ちょうどでの truncate は妥当な短い台帳になり内容だけでは検出不能）は known-gap テストとして明示的に固定した。 v0.2.15: `audit-round record` now REFUSES a round whose CONFIRMED findings are not closed by regression tests (`regression_tests_added < confirmed`) — non-zero exit, nothing written to the ledger — and `scripts/continuous-audit.sh` stops there instead of swallowing it via the fail-soft `run_ow` wrapper (a new `run_ow_gate` is used for verdict-bearing calls, so the refusal is not inert). The continuous-audit SKILL.md gains a MANDATORY Step 3.5 mirror sweep (polarity / axis / alternate spelling / other writers to the same store / granularity) and drops the 「record 時は 0 のままにしてよい」 allowance that let a round record confirmed:10 with regression_tests_added:0 (round 2026W29), which is why new_findings oscillated 5→1→13→0→14→15 at converging:false. closure_rate becomes an acceptance precondition rather than a metric for new rounds; `converging` does not read it, so convergence does not become easier to satisfy. v0.2.14: fixes `cargo fmt --check -p overwatch` drift in `src/store.rs` and `tests/review_queue.rs` (multi-line `match`/`return` and `.expect()` line-wrap formatting); formatting only, no logic change. v0.2.13: `skills/continuous-audit/SKILL.md`'s "既定の target" list now names `taintguard` alongside the other GATE crates (kept in sync with `scripts/continuous-audit.sh`'s `DEFAULT_TARGETS`, which now also carries it — taintguard joined GATE_CRATES in this same change). v0.2.6: `skills/continuous-audit/SKILL.md`'s REFUTED-default-bias rationale (why-block, 2026-07-21 specguard forge/gather.rs incident) now links to CLAUDE.md §6 instead of independently re-deriving it (docs/gate-taxonomy.md now also documents which GATE_CRATES members block immediately (blastguard/propguard) vs. protect-the-protector without blocking (mutategate/stuckguard/specguard/overwatch), verified against each crate's own hooks/hooks.json). v0.2.5: extends the cross-gate violation ledger — `ViolationSource` gains 6 new ingest sources (Donegate/Reviewgate/Tdd/Budgetguard/Autoflow/Ctxrot) plus a shared `check_kind: Option<&str>` field on `RawViolation` for gates whose blocking reason reduces to one short discriminator (unlike blastguard's structured `rule_id` or specguard's `drift_kind`+`symbol` pair); `normalize_signature` routes all 6 through `check_kind`. v0.2.0 (major bump, not content): 0.1.52 added pub fields to externally-constructible structs (`AuditRound.unverified`, `RoundMetric.unverified`, `AuditMetrics.cumulative_unverified`, `ReviewFinding.verdict`) without a breaking version bump, so `cargo semver-checks` correctly failed CI on main (17 consecutive runs) with `constructible_struct_adds_field`; this release only bumps 0.1→0.2 per the crate's own pre-1.0 convention (breaking change bumps the minor field) to match the version to the API shape already shipped — no code change. v0.1.52: `test_freshness`'s reverse-lookup source walk now fails closed on an incomplete scan (50ad2c1e, twin of specguard testaudit/gather rounds #7/#11): `rust_source_files` returns `io::Result` (a MISSING dir/root is a legitimate empty, but an EXISTING-but-unreadable dir, a per-entry listing error, or an unreadable `.rs`/`Cargo.toml` is INCOMPLETE → `Err`), and `find_ignored_test` returns a tri-state `IgnoredTestLookup{Found,NotFound,ScanIncomplete}` instead of `Option`. `bridge.rs` maps `ScanIncomplete` to the new `TestFreshness::ScanIncomplete` and renders it as a distinct "判定不能（走査未完）" triage line rather than folding it into "該当テストなし" — an unreadable subtree that might hold a finding's regression test no longer masquerades as a false "no test" deprioritize signal. The old `let Ok(read_dir) else {continue}` + `entries.flatten()` swallows are gone, and the two grandfathered check-fail-open.py ALLOWLIST entries were removed with them. v0.1.48: `store::mark_branch_merged` (branch-keyed sibling of `mark_changeset_merged`) + `store::clear_runtime_overlap_holds` give condukt the on-land cleanup that takes a merged branch's changeset out of the mid-flight overlap set (fixing spurious ~30-min false-positive merge HOLDs) and clears stale RuntimeOverlap holds; `prune_stale_changesets` wired opportunistically keeps `active_changesets.json` bounded. All fail-soft under `LeaseLock`. v0.1.47: runtime conflict detection + consensus merge-conflict store (design 625aa170). New `changeset.rs` holds a project-global in-flight actual-changeset registry (`ActualChangeset`) + a runtime-conflict stream; `store::record_changeset_and_detect` (LeaseLock RMW) detects a mid-flight actual-diff overlap between two in-flight worktrees and appends a `RuntimeConflictEvent`. New `merge_conflict.rs` + store streams hold blocked-merge entries (`MergeConflictEntry`: origin MergeConflict|RuntimeOverlap, conflicted files, both byte-bounded diffs) and their resolutions (`MergeConflictResolution`, joined by conflict_id; OPEN set = unresolved); `review-queue` gains a `[merge-conflict]` High-severity kind so a held/blocked merge surfaces in the same unified human review pane and drains to backlog. New `overwatch resolve-merge-conflict --id <id> --choose ours|theirs|manual` writes a resolution (RMW under LeaseLock, idempotent). All detection/compute is fail-soft. v0.1.44: `lease::begin()`'s load->is_held_by_other check->save read-modify-write was unprotected against a TOCTOU race (two sessions racing begin() for the same key could both pass the check before either saved, both believing they'd claimed the lease) -- condukt::lock/backlog::lock had already fixed this exact pattern via hardlink+create_new(O_EXCL) exclusive locking, but overwatch::lease hadn't (hypothesis 9c733d74). New `crates/overwatch/src/lock.rs` (`LeaseLock`) ports that design -- hard-link atomic publish, a TMP_SEQ intra-process collision guard, stale-lock reap via pid liveness, bounded wait, fail-soft degrade-to-unlocked on timeout -- and `begin()` now holds it across the whole load->check->save cycle. New `crates/overwatch/tests/lease_concurrency.rs` spawns two real processes racing `begin()` for the same key across 8 trials and asserts exactly one wins; an env-gated `OVERWATCH_TEST_BEGIN_DELAY_MS` widens the race window past normal process-spawn overhead so the test deterministically forces the interleave (verified by temporarily reverting the lock: the test then reliably catches the double-claim). Also fixed a related pre-existing test-suite flake: `aggregate.rs` and `store.rs` each sandboxed the process-global `$HOME` env var behind their OWN separate `Mutex`, so tests in the two modules could still race each other's `HOME` mutation under parallel `cargo test`; unified to one crate-wide `store::HOME_ENV_LOCK`. v0.1.43: `review-metrics` now reports `stale_undisposed_with_fix_commit` — a read-only recount (same commit-range/store logic as `reconcile-fixed`, but never writes) of findings whose fix commit has already landed but are still undisposed, printed as a WARNING line in the human-readable report too. Closes the last piece of the 2026-07-17 stale-review-queue gap: `reconcile-fixed` only clears the backlog when someone remembers to run it, so this makes the gap visible on every `review-metrics` call even if reconcile-fixed hasn't run that round. v0.1.42: new `reconcile-fixed` command closes the "fix commit landed, nobody ran record-disposition" gap that let review-queue go stale (2026-07-17 incident: 18 already-fixed findings sat "open" for weeks because nobody remembered to dispose them). Scans a range of git commit messages (`--since-ref`/`--range`/`--last-n`, default last 50) for `CA-<crate>-<NNN>` finding-id references and auto-records a CONFIRMED disposition (`auto-reconcile(commit <hash>)`) for any referenced finding present on the review-findings store but not yet dispositioned; idempotent (already-disposed ids are skipped, a finding referenced by multiple commits is disposed once). Fail-soft end-to-end: a missing git binary, a non-repo cwd, or a non-zero `git log` all degrade to "0 processed" rather than erroring, so it is always safe to wire into automation. Wired into `scripts/continuous-audit.sh` (via the existing fail-soft `run_ow` wrapper) so every Continuous-Audit round auto-reconciles already-fixed findings before bridging the remainder to the backlog. v0.1.39: `test_freshness::run_ignored_test`'s `cargo test` subprocess call used `Command::output()`, which waits unbounded — a hung/deadlocking `#[ignore]`d regression test could wedge `overwatch review-queue --to-backlog`'s per-finding loop forever. Switched to `spawn()` + `wait_timeout()` (60s, since the call includes a build step) mirroring `ctxrot::hooks::guard::run_with_timeout`; timeout kills and reaps the child, folding into the existing `ExecutionError` fail-soft path (`bridge.rs` unchanged). review-queue → backlog consolidation: `review-queue --to-backlog` now drains the WHOLE unified queue (ai-finding / systemic / rollback / escalation), not just AI findings — each not-yet-bridged entry is forwarded via `backlog add` so `/flow` can auto-repair it. The three non-finding streams are keyed on a composite `<kind>:<identifier>` in a separate `bridged_entries.jsonl` ledger so the finding-resolution source (`bridged_findings.jsonl`) is untouched; systemic/rollback/escalation ride one priority tier hotter (p0) and are tagged with their kind for filterability. Fail-soft throughout (missing store / absent backlog / failed add are warned and skipped; exit 0). Fixed CA-overwatch-004: AuditRound::new (the constructor the audit-round `record` CLI path uses) now clamps regression_tests_added to confirmed for every construction path, not just the separate close-path set_round_tests, so `audit-round record --confirmed N --regression-tests-added M` can no longer persist or report a closure_rate above the documented [0,1] range. continuous-audit SKILL.md's target-crate default doc now matches the real 6-crate DEFAULT_TARGETS (overwatch included) instead of understating 5. set_round_tests() clamps an over-large --tests count to the round's own confirmed count before storing, so audit-round close can never push closure_rate above the documented [0,1] range. Project-global cross-session execution ledger with dedup guard + PDO progress view. Manages claim registry with heartbeat-based liveness and skip-on-duplicate contract for distributed session coordination. SessionStart and Stop hooks surface current run state and progress aggregation (session/backlog/hypothesis/condukt run/compass gap in fail-soft view) via a short-lived (10s TTL) on-disk render cache, so the two hooks firing close together collapse into one full aggregate scan (~5 subprocess spawns) instead of two; a cold/expired/corrupt cache always falls through to a fresh build (fail-soft). Includes the /continuous-audit driver skill that runs an adversarial finder->verifier review round over the gate crates and auto-populates the unified review-queue (findings deduped by content fingerprint, not just id; repeated same-plugin rollbacks likewise collapse, each with an occurrences count). review-queue now also bridges condukt's durable escalation queue in fail-soft by path (`EntryKind::Escalation`, High severity) so blocked/GATED tasks awaiting a human answer show in the same unified pane. New `auto-approved` companion command surfaces the auto-approved (self-answered without a human) decision population from condukt's `gate-decisions.jsonl`, fail-soft by path, as a count plus a deterministic seeded sample, so sampling coverage of mass auto-approval stays auditable. `record-disposition`/`review-metrics` close the loop with review-effectiveness measurement (false-positive rate, human-agreement rate, median resolution latency); the integration tests now patch only the CLI-written ledgers' timestamp fields, keeping the CLI-serialized verdict/reviewer intact, so those assertions cover record-disposition's field serialization end-to-end. New `compact-findings` command performs non-lossy compaction/rotation of the append-only review_findings.jsonl hot store: resolved (bridged or dispositioned) findings are MOVED into a cold review_findings_archive.jsonl (atomic temp+rename, archive written before hot for crash-safety, idempotent) so review-queue's human-surface read stays bounded to OPEN items while review-metrics keeps joining archived findings via the combined hot-plus-archive history. Continuous-Audit finding triage: `ReviewFinding` gains an optional `rationale` field (the verifier's CONFIRMED rationale, `#[serde(default)]` for backward-compatible reads) wired through `record-finding --rationale`; a new `test_freshness` module reverse-looks-up a `#[ignore = "<finding-id>: ..."]` regression test by finding-id and re-runs it fail-soft (Passing/Failing/NotFound/ExecutionError); `review-queue --to-backlog` now thickens each backlog task's notes with elapsed days since confirmation, the rationale (if any), and the regression-test freshness verdict, all advisory-only. Subscription-native (skill + hook + bundled Rust binary, no API key).

plugins.name: daily
plugins.description: Daily-once task runner for Claude Code: a SessionStart hook that runs registered shell tasks ([[task]] in ~/.daily/config.toml) at most once per calendar day and injects a summary of what ran. Skips while a /flow or /backlog driver is working (backlog lock), records each run to a JSONL report (a failed task still counts as run, no retry until tomorrow). task.command is checked against blastguard before spawning; a flagged command is refused fail-closed and reported as blocked. With no tasks registered it runs a default security audit (cargo deny check). Register/inspect with `daily add` / `daily list` / `daily report`. Subscription-native (one hook + bundled Rust binary, no API key).

plugins.name: scout
plugins.description: Multi-lens project audit that generates actionable tasks (施策) for Claude Code: a /scout skill that gathers deterministic project state, fans out read-only sub-agents across five lenses (current issues, security, industry/peer-project practices via web search, missing measures, safety), then dedupes/scores findings into prioritized tasks, writes them to the backlog, and hands execution to /flow. Complements compass as a broad-reconnaissance SOURCE. Subscription-native (skill only, no binary, no API key). v0.1.3: Phase 5's backlog add convention now also references docs/backlog-tag-taxonomy.md for cross-project work-category tags.

plugins.name: daily-report
plugins.description: Generates a scannable daily work report (日報) by aggregating the day's git commits and the Obsidian session records that session-insights writes to the vault, then synthesizing them into a single narrative note written back to <vault>/daily/<date>.md. git supplies what changed in this repo; the Obsidian records supply cross-project summaries/learnings/remaining tasks and cost/token numbers. Subscription-native (skill only, no binary, no API key).

plugins.name: trajectoryeval
plugins.description: Trajectory-match verifier for agent tool-call paths: condukt's online verifier checks a task's OUTPUT (done_criteria); trajectoryeval checks the PATH the worker took. `check` matches an actual ordered tool-call list against an expected trajectory spec (strict / unordered / subsequence) and reports {pass, missing, unexpected, out_of_order} with a 0/1/2 gate exit; `extract` streams a transcript into the ordered tool_use names. The path-side sibling of done-criteria verification (agentevals-style). Subscription-native (one bundled Rust binary, no API key).

plugins.name: replaykit
plugins.description: Trace→golden replay regression harness: turns a tracekit-recorded condukt run into an evalkit golden case so a real run becomes a committed regression fixture. `extract` distils a run's spans.jsonl into a portable trajectory summary (ordered phase/model/status steps + an `expect` block pinning phase set / error count / cost); `promote` writes the fixture under evals/replay/fixtures and appends a dedup'd golden whose `cmd` re-runs `replaykit verify`; `verify` recomputes those aggregates from the steps and gates 0/1/2. The trace-side sibling of curate's playbook→golden. Subscription-native (one bundled Rust binary, file-only, no network, no API key).

plugins.name: propguard
plugins.description: Property gate for Claude Code: on Stop, derive 3–5 semantic properties (invariants) from a task's done_criteria and check the generated code against them before the agent can declare done. In inject mode it blocks and injects a property checklist for the running agent to self-verify (no API key); in subprocess mode it runs an independent checker and counts per-property PASS/FAIL, blocking when fewer than a threshold hold. Goes beyond 'concrete tests pass'. v0.1.32: fixed a stale never-break-a-turn docstring/comment in main.rs and README.md — panics no longer swallow-to-exit-0; the Stop hook's panic path resolves via harness_core::gate::run::run_guarded's fail-closed policy (block on the first stop, bounded allow only on a second consecutive stop_hook_active panic). No behavior change. v0.1.31: migrated run_checker's and run_git's independently-duplicated spawn+process-group-kill+bounded-timeout+bounded-stdout-read logic (CA-propguard-004/005/006) to the new shared harness_core::boundary::run_with_timeout / run_with_timeout_and_stdin primitive; local kill_checker_tree/kill_tree/read_stdout_bounded helpers removed, propguard's own wait-timeout dependency dropped (libc kept only for a test-only liveness probe). Existing timeout/kill/parse behavior preserved (all regression tests green). v0.1.29: cargo fmt fixup of a test fixture in derive.rs (no behavior change). v0.1.28: migrated 3 raw fs::read_to_string call sites (Config::load, source_criteria, diff_text's untracked-file read) to harness_core::boundary::read_to_string so an unreadable-but-existing file is distinguished from a genuinely absent one instead of both being silently folded together; existing fallback behavior at each site is unchanged. v0.1.27: fixed README.ja.md's stale doctrine — panics no longer swallow-to-exit-0; they resolve via harness_core::gate::run::run_guarded's fail-closed policy (block on first panic, bounded allow only on a second consecutive stop_hook_active panic). v0.1.16: merged two independently-developed Continuous-Audit fix lines that landed on the same v0.1.14 base — stopped correlation-store pollution (CA-propguard-03/04), and documented the checker subprocess timeout (checker_timeout_secs, default 300s, process-tree kill on timeout) with config-propagation tests. v0.1.13: fixed 3 subprocess-hang gaps (CA-propguard-004/005/006) — checker timeout now kills the whole shell-spawned process tree via a Unix process group, stdout reads are bounded so a lingering process can't hang them, and all git subprocess calls go through a timeout-bounded choke point with graceful fallback. Subscription-native, bundled Rust binary.

plugins.name: taintguard
plugins.description: v0.1.6: state::Check::Undetermined now ENFORCES REGARDLESS OF POSTURE — a corrupt/wrong-schema taint marker, or an unwritable state dir, resolves to ask/deny even under TAINTGUARD_OBSERVE_ONLY=1. Through 0.1.5 observe-only suppressed Undetermined as well, i.e. 'I could not determine the taint state' was silenced by a measurement flag — exactly the cannot-determine→permissive collapse CLAUDE.md §3 forbids. Rationale for the asymmetry (Tainted + observe-only STILL suppresses; that is unchanged): observe-only exists to measure the friction caused by KNOWN taint, and an Undetermined check names no sources at all (its sources array is empty), so suppressing it buys no measurement while spending the §3 invariant — 'could not determine' is the same class as 'panicked', and the panic barrier already enforced regardless of posture. Deliberate ledger decision, made explicit in code comments and in README.ja.md: an enforced-Undetermined under observe-only appends NO ledger line, because the ledger and `taintguard tally`'s `suppressed` field are defined as *suppressed enforcements* and this event was not suppressed — folding it in would make a counter whose name asserts suppression lie, and splitting `suppressed` three ways would change tally's output contract, which is out of scope for this change. The event stays visible as the ask/deny it actually produces, whose reason text now carries observe::undetermined_not_suppressed_note (replacing the now-unreachable observe::warning_undetermined, whose prose described a suppression that no longer happens) telling the operator that observe-only is set but is NOT honoured on this path and that no ledger line was written. New ledger records therefore always carry check: "tainted"; the field is kept rather than dropped because ledgers written by <=0.1.5 can contain "undetermined" lines that must still parse. The decisive test is end-to-end against the REAL binary with the REAL env var in tests/provenance_gate.rs — not a unit test on decide_gate_with, since a prior fault-injection audit proved the unit tests there are blind (observe::posture() is the only reader of TAINTGUARD_OBSERVE_ONLY and had zero test callers, so a loose env parse stayed green across the whole suite) — and the pre-existing E2E test that pinned the old behaviour, whose own docstring had flagged this §3 conflict as 'a design decision for a human', is rewritten rather than deleted. Anti-vacuity is asserted in the same suite: Tainted + observe-only still emits no permissionDecision and still appends exactly one ledger line, so this change is distinguishable from deleting observe-only wholesale. v0.1.5: acts on an adversarial re-verification of 0.1.4, which found that the commit fixing prose-vs-reality had left four instances of the same defect class behind. `src/lib.rs` still said "Three hooks, three subcommands" after 0.1.4 added a fourth (main.rs's header was updated in the same commit, lib.rs was not); `bin/taintguard`'s fallback comment still said "no other subcommand exists", which `tally` falsified; `hookio::context_json` had ZERO production callers once emit_gate switched to observe_json, yet the unit test whose docstring claimed to pin observe-only's no-permissionDecision shape still exercised that dead function — precisely the all-call-sites-are-#[cfg(test)] defect 0.1.4 indicted in observe::tally — so the test now serializes through observe_json (and additionally asserts the top-level systemMessage is not nested) and context_json is removed. Also corrects a FALSE sentence in tally's own output: a DANGLING SYMLINK at the ledger path opens ENOENT, which harness_core::boundary maps to absent, so tally printed "the ledger was read successfully and holds no records" with exit 0 when nothing had been opened at all; the zero-case line now claims only what is true (no records AND no read error), which is the part that distinguishes it from the non-zero-exit failure path. Finally, three tests resolved "the fault could not be injected" (chmod 000 under root; a directory that could not be planted) to `return` — which cargo reports as a PASS while hiding the explanatory stderr note, rendering "I could not verify" indistinguishable from "I verified it". Per CLAUDE.md §3 cannot-determine now resolves to the restricted side: those sites panic, so the suite goes red rather than silently stopping covering the fail-open it exists to pin. Absolute-absence wording about additionalContext was also pulled back to the docs' actual claim ("doesn't appear as a chat message in the interface"), and the README now documents the ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/taintguard invocation. v0.1.4: makes the observe-only measurement actually RETRIEVABLE and corrects prose that overstated its visibility. v0.1.3 asserted 「沈黙はしない」 ("it does not stay silent") and justified observe-only's safety with that claim, but per the Claude Code hooks reference (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.md) `additionalContext` is wrapped in a system reminder and injected into Claude's context and "doesn't appear as a chat message in the interface" — it is a MODEL-facing channel, so to a human the mode was in fact indistinguishable from a gate that found nothing (a CLAUDE.md §4 prose-vs-behaviour defect). Worse, `observe::tally` had NO production consumer at all: all four call sites were inside #[cfg(test)], and the Command enum was only Mark/Gate/Clear, so the number the whole feature exists to produce could not be read back through the tool. This release adds a `taintguard tally` subcommand as the GUARANTEED human readout: it prints the ledger path plus separately-parseable `suppressed:` and `corrupt:` counts (`--json` emits exactly {ledger,suppressed,corrupt} with numeric values), and it is deliberately NOT wrapped in harness_core::hook::run_hook because that helper ends in exit(0) — an unreadable ledger must exit NON-ZERO with the propagated 'could not read' text plus 'NOT a tally of zero' on stderr and print no count anywhere, while a genuinely absent ledger is a real 0 that additionally prints 'nothing observed yet' so the two are distinguishable in the OUTPUT and not merely by exit code (a failure to resolve the process cwd is likewise non-zero, never a zero tally). A top-level `systemMessage` (sibling of hookSpecificOutput, never nested inside it) now also carries the suppression warning, but it is BEST-EFFORT ONLY and nothing depends on it: the docs contain no example pairing `systemMessage` with a PreToolUse response that omits `permissionDecision`, so its behaviour on a non-blocking response is UNDOCUMENTED. `permissionDecision` is still omitted entirely — NOT switched to 'allow', since an explicit allow is a positive verdict that would override other gates and the user's own permission rules. This release also closes two live fail-opens an independent fault-injection audit proved the 66-test suite was blind to: `observe::posture()` (the ONLY reader of TAINTGUARD_OBSERVE_ONLY) had zero test callers, so a loose truthy parse there left the suite fully green while TAINTGUARD_OBSERVE_ONLY=false silently DISABLED the gate; and deleting the println! in emit_gate's Observe arm also left the suite green, making a suppressed enforcement byte-identical to a clean turn on stdout. Five new end-to-end tests drive the REAL binary and the REAL env var (not observe::resolve, which was the bypass that hid the first fault), and each was confirmed to catch its specific injected fault; three pre-existing tests whose docstrings claimed properties their bodies never checked were corrected rather than deleted. v0.1.3: adds an opt-in observe-only (warn-only) MEASUREMENT posture so the gate's friction can be OBSERVED before it is enabled fleet-wide — previously the only two options were 'enforce' and 'not installed', so 'how much would this get in the way?' was answerable only by prediction. `TAINTGUARD_OBSERVE_ONLY=1` makes `gate` emit NO permissionDecision (so nothing is enforced — this setting DISABLES the protection and is for measurement only) while still emitting a visible hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext warning naming the taint, its sources, and the fact that enforcement was suppressed, plus one append-only JSONL line per suppressed enforcement at <project_key>/observe-only.jsonl (project-scoped, not session-scoped, since the Stop hook's clear wipes session markers and a per-session rate is not the number wanted). Deliberately NOT permissionDecision=allow — an explicit allow is a positive verdict that would OVERRIDE other gates and the user's own permission rules, so a mode whose purpose is to stop enforcing would end up enforcing something broader. Not a fail-open by construction: observe-only is a fourth DECLARED state ('checked, and intentionally did not enforce') kept on a separate axis (observe::Posture) from state::Check, so no path can turn a Tainted/Undetermined check into a Clean one and the suppressed finding stays countable; the opt-in fails closed on every unrecognised value (unset/empty/0/false/true/space-1/01/typos all enforce — no trimming, no case-folding, no truthy parsing — and Posture has no Default impl); a panic still fails closed to ask/deny even under observe-only (a panic means the posture read itself did not complete, so cannot-determine resolves to the restricted side regardless of posture); and the ledger tally reports parseable and CORRUPT line counts separately so a damaged ledger cannot quietly under-report the rate. Also refactored the gate panic barrier to be parameterised (analyse_gate_barrier) so the panic-barrier tests now drive the real production barrier instead of a look-alike copy that had lived in the test module (a regression in the real barrier would previously have failed no test), and unified the two per-module TAINTGUARD_STATE_DIR test locks into one crate-wide lock (two independent locks did not exclude each other). Every new claim was verified by fault injection rather than assertion alone: 8 deliberate faults (collapse observe-only to Silent, any-value opt-in, permissionDecision=allow, swallowed ledger write error, undetermined folded into tainted, warn on clean turns, panic honouring observe-only, corrupt ledger lines silently ignored) were each observed RED before the corrected code was confirmed GREEN. v0.1.2: adds the crates/taintguard/bin/taintguard launcher this plugin previously shipped without (backlog 4ee2b335) — enabledPlugins could not activate it at all until now, since hooks.json execs bin/<crate>, never the compiled binary directly. Missing-binary fallback follows the ctxrot-corrected pattern: `gate` (PreToolUse, verdict-bearing) resolves to permissionDecision=ask rather than staying silent (silence reads as an allow); `mark`/`clear` (state-mutation, no verdict channel) are non-silent-but-exit-0. Also added to GATE_CRATES (requires --canary rollout) and to check-plugin-rollout.py's new detection for a GATE crate declaring a binary target with no repo-side bin/ launcher. v0.1.1: closes an independently-verified fail-open — an absent taint marker after a lost/unpersisted mark (state dir readable-but-unwritable) used to read as Clean/allow indistinguishably from a genuinely clean session; `gate`'s absent-marker branch now probes the session state dir's writability before trusting the absence (probe succeeds → Clean/allow unchanged, probe fails → Undetermined → ask/deny), with a control test proving a healthy writable empty store still allows silently. Also: a valid-JSON but wrong-schema marker (missing the required `tainted` field) now fails closed to Undetermined instead of serde-defaulting to Clean; an unresolved leading `~` in a Read target (`~/secret`) now classifies Untrusted instead of lexically-joining onto the root as Trusted; and a docstring that falsely claimed the absent-marker case already failed closed has been corrected to describe the actual (now fixed) behavior. New crate. Provenance-scoped least-privilege gate: after a turn consumes untrusted-provenance content (a WebFetch/WebSearch result, or a Read outside the project root), write-class tools (Bash/Write/Edit/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit) are downgraded to ask (interactive) / deny (headless) for the rest of that turn; a clean Stop restores normal access. Subscription-native, bundled Rust binary.

plugins.name: fetchguard
plugins.description: New crate (backlog 18506c09). Runtime content-level injection scanner: a PostToolUse hook (matcher WebFetch|WebSearch) scans the tool_response text for planted prompt-injection phrasings (concealment / verification-bypass / instruction-override / egress — the same four-category taxonomy scripts/check-prompt-injection.py already enforces at commit time) and, on a hit OR an undecidable response shape, injects additionalContext telling the model the flagged span is untrusted DATA whose embedded directives must NOT be followed. Closes the gap check-prompt-injection.py's own docstring names: that gate covers committed prompt assets, not text a web tool call pulls in at runtime. Orthogonal to taintguard's provenance signal (WHERE content came from) — this is the content signal (WHAT it says); the two are meant to run together. External-file Read is deferred (needs taintguard's path-trust classifier). A shared fixture corpus (scripts/tests/fixtures/injection_parity_corpus.json) is run by both this crate's tests/pattern_parity.rs and scripts/test_check_prompt_injection.py's ParityWithFetchguardCorpus, so the two independently-maintained taxonomies cannot silently drift apart. Subscription-native, bundled Rust binary (not yet registered in any enabledPlugins — building/merging this crate has no effect on a running session until a human does so and restarts).
